```html
<main>
  <section id="code">
    <div class="wrap">
      <h2>Nearly a third of the functions are about people</h2>
      <p class="prose">The program holds about 43,000 functions that we can read. Sorted by what they work on, the largest group by far belongs to pedestrians: how they decide, react, walk and fight.</p>
      <ol class="bars" aria-label="Functions by subsystem">
        <li style="--v:13286"><span class="bar-label">People: AI tasks and events</span><span class="bar-track"><span class="bar-fill"></span></span><span class="bar-value">13,286</span></li>
        <li style="--v:4419"><span class="bar-label">Timing, locking, start-up</span><span class="bar-track"><span class="bar-fill"></span></span><span class="bar-value">4,419</span></li>
        <li style="--v:4416"><span class="bar-label">Streaming and loading</span><span class="bar-track"><span class="bar-fill"></span></span><span class="bar-value">4,416</span></li>
        <li style="--v:3261"><span class="bar-label">Files and memory</span><span class="bar-track"><span class="bar-fill"></span></span><span class="bar-value">3,261</span></li>
        <li style="--v:3240"><span class="bar-label">Physics and collision</span><span class="bar-track"><span class="bar-fill"></span></span><span class="bar-value">3,240</span></li>
        <li style="--v:2974"><span class="bar-label">Input, menus and HUD</span><span class="bar-track"><span class="bar-fill"></span></span><span class="bar-value">2,974</span></li>
        <li style="--v:2893"><span class="bar-label">Network and online</span><span class="bar-track"><span class="bar-fill"></span></span><span class="bar-value">2,893</span></li>
        <li style="--v:2863"><span class="bar-label">Script machine and natives</span><span class="bar-track"><span class="bar-fill"></span></span><span class="bar-value">2,863</span></li>
        <li style="--v:2586"><span class="bar-label">Vehicles</span><span class="bar-track"><span class="bar-fill"></span></span><span class="bar-value">2,586</span></li>
        <li style="--v:2370"><span class="bar-label">Audio</span><span class="bar-track"><span class="bar-fill"></span></span><span class="bar-value">2,370</span></li>
        <li style="--v:1620"><span class="bar-label">World and object pools</span><span class="bar-track"><span class="bar-fill"></span></span><span class="bar-value">1,620</span></li>
        <li style="--v:1276"><span class="bar-label">Animation and Euphoria</span><span class="bar-track"><span class="bar-fill"></span></span><span class="bar-value">1,276</span></li>
      </ol>
      <p class="note">This counts functions, not bytes of code. Each function is assigned to the nearest subsystem whose code could be identified, so the split is approximate; 25 could not be placed. The bars were counted on the first inventory of 45,229 entries. A later repair removed 4,540 that were not functions and added 2,467 that had been missed, which changes the totals but not the picture. The counts include the libraries built into the program and leave out the megabyte that cannot be read yet. There is no rendering group because the survey behind these labels did not have one: rendering functions are spread across the groups above, and much of the low-level graphics code is in the unreadable megabyte.</p>

      <div class="split">
        <div>
          <h3>More than half of the classes are leaderboards</h3>
          <p>A class is a blueprint for one kind of object. The program declares 3,727 of them. About 1,927 are four leaderboard templates, each stamped out once for every one of 481 multiplayer leaderboards. The largest family that does real work is the AI's 334 task classes.</p>
          <ul class="waffle-key">
            <li><span class="key-swatch lb"></span>Leaderboard templates, 1,927</li>
            <li><span class="key-swatch task"></span>AI tasks, 334</li>
            <li><span class="key-swatch rest"></span>Everything else, 1,466</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
        <div class="waffle" id="waffle" role="img" aria-label="A grid of 100 squares: 52 are leaderboard templates, 9 are AI tasks and 39 are everything else."></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section id="people" class="band">
    <div class="wrap">
      <h2>A pedestrian thinks in layers</h2>
      <p class="prose">Nobody in Liberty City runs one big behaviour routine. Each person holds a goal, the goal picks a smaller step, and the step picks one action. When something happens nearby, an event arrives and can replace any of the three layers.</p>
      <div class="brain">
        <div class="brain-events">
          <strong>Events</strong>
          <span>A gunshot, damage, a shout. 82 kinds. An event can replace any layer.</span>
        </div>
        <ol class="layers">
          <li class="layer goal">
            <strong>Goal</strong>
            <span>A complex task. It chooses a step and watches it. 197 kinds of complex task.</span>
            <em>In plain words: get to the other side of the street.</em>
          </li>
          <li class="link to-step">picks</li>
          <li class="layer step">
            <strong>Step</strong>
            <span>Another complex task. Steps can nest several deep.</span>
            <em>Walk to the kerb.</em>
          </li>
          <li class="link to-action">picks</li>
          <li class="layer action">
            <strong>Action</strong>
            <span>A simple task. It does one thing for a few frames, then reports back. About 130 kinds.</span>
            <em>Take one stride.</em>
          </li>
          <li class="link to-action">drives</li>
          <li class="layer body">
            <strong>The body moves</strong>
            <span>Movement and animation, or Euphoria if the body goes limp.</span>
          </li>
        </ol>
      </div>
      <p class="note">The counts are measured from the program's class records. The street-crossing example is ours, to show the idea; it is not taken from the game's task names.</p>
      <ul class="facts">
        <li><strong>About 192 bytes</strong> is the typical size of a complex task. Tasks live in fixed pools, not in general-purpose memory.</li>
        <li><strong>39 movement tasks</strong> carry a second interface so the movement system can drive them directly.</li>
        <li><strong>18 Euphoria behaviours</strong> take over when a body turns ragdoll.</li>
        <li><strong>We found no "wanted level" class</strong> in the readable code. Police response appears to be driven by data files and scripts.</li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section id="scripts">
    <div class="wrap">
      <h2>The story runs on a small stack machine</h2>
      <p class="prose">Missions are not built into the program. They ship as 941 script files, run by an interpreter: a loop that reads one instruction at a time and carries it out. It knows 78 instructions and keeps its working numbers on a stack, like a pile of plates. Scripts cannot touch the engine directly. They call named commands, called natives, and the engine does the work.</p>
      <div class="vm" id="vm">
        <div class="vm-program">
          <h3>Program</h3>
          <ol class="vm-code" id="vm-code">
            <li>PUSH 5</li>
            <li>PUSH 7</li>
            <li>ADD</li>
          </ol>
        </div>
        <div class="vm-stack-wrap">
          <h3>Stack</h3>
          <div class="vm-stack" id="vm-stack" aria-live="polite"></div>
        </div>
        <div class="vm-controls">
          <p id="vm-status">Press Step to run the first instruction.</p>
          <button type="button" id="vm-step">Step</button>
          <button type="button" id="vm-reset" class="quiet">Start again</button>
        </div>
      </div>
      <p class="note">This three-instruction program was the first thing the project ran through the game's original interpreter code. It answered 12. A real script does the same thing with a native in place of ADD: push the arguments, call the native, read the answer off the stack.</p>
      <ul class="facts big">
        <li><strong>14,499,370</strong> instructions across all the shipped scripts.</li>
        <li><strong>717,139</strong> calls from scripts into the engine.</li>
        <li><strong>3,034</strong> natives registered, every one now named.</li>
      </ul>
      <ul class="facts">
        <li><strong>IS_CHAR_INJURED</strong> is the most-called native, followed by PRINTSTRING and IS_CHAR_DEAD.</li>
        <li><strong>Dividing by zero</strong> does not crash a script: the result is the number you started with.</li>
        <li><strong>46 debug natives</strong> were stripped from the release build and now all lead to one empty function.</li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section id="disk" class="band">
    <div class="wrap">
      <h2>The city is 23.9 GB of nested containers</h2>
      <p class="prose">Almost everything sits inside archives. Inside an archive, each model, texture set or collision mesh is a compressed resource, laid out so it can be copied into memory and used without further parsing.</p>
      <div class="disk-bar" role="img" aria-label="23.9 gigabytes: 10.2 in 49 RPF archives, 10.1 in 254 IMG archives, 3.6 in loose files and video.">
        <span class="seg rpf" style="--w:10.2"><b>10.2 GB</b> 49 archives of audio and models</span>
        <span class="seg img" style="--w:10.1"><b>10.1 GB</b> 254 encrypted map archives</span>
        <span class="seg loose" style="--w:3.6"><b>3.6 GB</b> video and loose files</span>
      </div>
      <div class="nesting">
        <div class="nest-box archive"><strong>Archive</strong><span>A table of contents and thousands of files. The map archives are encrypted with a key held in the program file.</span>
          <div class="nest-box resource"><strong>Resource</strong><span>One compressed file, split into a part for main memory and a part for the graphics card.</span>
            <div class="nest-box object"><strong>Object</strong><span>A model, texture set, collision mesh or navigation mesh, ready to use once the addresses inside it are corrected.</span></div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <ul class="facts big">
        <li><strong>26,713</strong> model files.</li>
        <li><strong>15.5 million</strong> collision polygons in 9,102 shapes.</li>
        <li><strong>10,839</strong> navigation meshes holding 5.65 million polygons.</li>
        <li><strong>95,137</strong> road nodes joined by 159,902 links.</li>
        <li><strong>10,134</strong> shader programs, all compiled ahead of time.</li>
        <li><strong>7</strong> languages of text.</li>
      </ul>
      <p class="note">The project's Rust readers open every one of these file types with no failures. The model reader is checked against a sample of 112 files so far.</p>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section id="clock">
    <div class="wrap">
      <h2>The clock counts in whole milliseconds</h2>
      <p class="prose">The engine reads a millisecond clock from more than 80 places and a high-resolution timer from one. We found no fixed step in the physics: the step follows the length of the frame. At 30 frames per second a millisecond is a fine ruler. At several hundred it is not.</p>
      <div class="clock" id="clock-widget">
        <div class="clock-top">
          <label for="fps">Frame rate: <output id="fps-out" for="fps">60</output> frames per second</label>
          <div class="presets" role="group" aria-label="Common frame rates">
            <button type="button" data-fps="30">30</button>
            <button type="button" data-fps="60">60</button>
            <button type="button" data-fps="144">144</button>
            <button type="button" data-fps="240">240</button>
          </div>
        </div>
        <input type="range" id="fps" min="20" max="500" step="1" value="60">
        <p class="ruler-caption">One frame, start to end. Each tick is one millisecond.</p>
        <div class="ruler" id="ruler" aria-hidden="true"></div>
        <p class="clock-readout" id="clock-readout" aria-live="polite"></p>
        <p class="ruler-key" id="ruler-key"><span class="key-swatch leftover"></span>The fraction of a millisecond at the end of the frame, which a whole-millisecond clock cannot see.</p>
      </div>
      <p class="note">Which of the two clocks paces the frame is in the code we cannot read yet, so this ruler illustrates a risk. It is not a measured cause. What is public record: players report that handling, ragdolls, helicopter rotors and ladders misbehave above 60 frames per second.</p>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section id="dark" class="band">
    <div class="wrap">
      <h2>One megabyte is still dark</h2>
      <p class="prose">The first megabyte of the game's code is encrypted in the file on disk and is only decrypted when the game starts. That is about 9% of the code, and it holds some of the most central parts.</p>
      <div class="strip" role="img" aria-label="The code as a strip of 2,674 pages: the first 250 are encrypted, the remaining 2,424 are readable.">
        <span class="strip-dark" style="--w:250"></span>
        <span class="strip-clear" style="--w:2424"></span>
      </div>
      <ul class="strip-key">
        <li><span class="key-swatch dark"></span>Encrypted on disk: 250 pages, 9%</li>
        <li><span class="key-swatch clear"></span>Readable: 2,424 pages</li>
      </ul>
      <p class="prose">Inside the dark part, as far as the readable code's references show:</p>
      <ul class="facts">
        <li><strong>The main loop</strong> and the program's real starting point.</li>
        <li><strong>The memory allocator</strong> that every object is created through.</li>
        <li><strong>98.8%</strong> of the virtual functions of the multiplayer replication classes.</li>
        <li><strong>83%</strong> of the virtual functions of the core classes: file devices, memory, parsing.</li>
        <li><strong>92 to 98%</strong> of those of the low-level graphics classes.</li>
        <li><strong>63%</strong> of those of the AI's event classes.</li>
      </ul>
      <p class="prose after-grid">The plan is to read that megabyte from the owner's running copy of the game, then repeat the analysis on it. Every number on this page comes from an entry in the <a href="devlog.html">devlog</a>, where the method and the open questions are written down.</p>
    </div>
  </section>
</main>
```

```js
      title: "Unpack",
      text: "Each file inside an archive is a compressed resource in two parts: one for main memory, one for the graphics card. After decompression the addresses inside it are corrected and it is usable as it stands.",
      facts: [["2", "parts in every resource"], ["zlib", "compression"]],
      measured: "checked on every loose resource file in the game folder."
    },
    world: {
      title: "Into the world",
      text: "Loaded objects take a slot in a fixed-size pool for their type. Far-away pedestrians are held as cheap stand-ins and swapped for the full version when the player gets close.",
      facts: [["26,713", "model files to draw from"]],
      measured: "pool-full error messages and the stand-in classes.",
      inferred: "the order of the stops on this line."
    }
  };
  var LINE_NAMES = { game: "Game thread", render: "Render thread", audio: "Audio", loader: "Streaming" };

  var panel = document.getElementById("stop-detail");
  var aside = document.getElementById("map-aside");
  var narrow = window.matchMedia("(max-width: 1200px)");
  var buttons = Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll(".stop"));
  var lines = Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll(".line"));
  var seen = {};
  var current = null;

  function evidence(id, label, value) {
    var node = document.getElementById(id);
    node.textContent = "";
    if (!value) return;
    var b = document.createElement("b");
    b.textContent = label + ": ";
    node.appendChild(b);
    node.appendChild(document.createTextNode(value));
  }

  function place(button) {
    var line = button.closest(".line");
    panel.style.setProperty("--line", getComputedStyle(line).getPropertyValue("--line"));
    (narrow.matches ? button.parentNode : aside).appendChild(panel);
  }

  function select(button, fromUser) {
    var stop = STOPS[button.dataset.stop];
    if (!stop) return;
    var before = button.getBoundingClientRect().top;
    var line = button.closest(".line");
    line.open = true;
    buttons.forEach(function (b) { b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", "false"); });
    button.setAttribute("aria-pressed", "true");
    if (fromUser) {
      button.classList.add("seen");
      seen[button.dataset.stop] = true;
    }
    current = button;
    document.getElementById("stop-line").textContent = LINE_NAMES[line.dataset.line];
    document.getElementById("stop-title").textContent = stop.title;
    document.getElementById("stop-text").textContent = stop.text;
    var facts = document.getElementById("stop-facts");
    facts.textContent = "";
    stop.facts.forEach(function (fact) {
      var li = document.createElement("li");
      var strong = document.createElement("strong");
      strong.textContent = fact[0];
      li.appendChild(strong);
      li.appendChild(document.createTextNode(" " + fact[1]));
      facts.appendChild(li);
    });
    evidence("stop-measured", "Measured", stop.measured);
    evidence("stop-inferred", "Inferred", stop.inferred);
    var more = document.getElementById("stop-more");
    document.getElementById("stop-more-row").hidden = !stop.more;
    if (stop.more) {
      more.href = stop.more[0];
      more.textContent = stop.more[1];
    }
    document.getElementById("stop-count").textContent = Object.keys(seen).length + " of " + buttons.length + " stops seen";
    place(button);
    panel.hidden = false;
    if (fromUser && narrow.matches) {
      // The panel moved, so content above the pressed stop may have changed height: keep the stop where it was.
      window.scrollBy(0, button.getBoundingClientRect().top - before);
      panel.scrollIntoView({ block: "nearest" });
    }
  }

  buttons.forEach(function (button) {
    button.setAttribute("aria-pressed", "false");
    button.addEventListener("click", function () { select(button, true); });
  });
  document.getElementById("stop-next").addEventListener("click", function () {
    var next = buttons[(buttons.indexOf(current) + 1) % buttons.length];
    select(next, true);
    if (narrow.matches) next.focus();
  });

  // On wide screens every line stays open; on narrow ones they are collapsible and only the first starts open.
  function layout() {
    lines.forEach(function (line, index) {
      line.open = narrow.matches ? (index === 0 || line.contains(current)) : true;
      line.querySelector("summary").tabIndex = narrow.matches ? 0 : -1;
    });
    if (current) place(current);
  }
  lines.forEach(function (line) {
    line.querySelector("summary").addEventListener("click", function (event) {
      if (!narrow.matches) event.preventDefault();
    });
  });
  narrow.addEventListener("change", layout);
  select(document.querySelector('.stop[data-stop="scripts"]'), false);
  layout();

  // Class grid: 100 squares, each about 37 classes.
  var waffle = document.getElementById("waffle");
  for (var i = 0; i < 100; i++) {
    var cell = document.createElement("span");
    cell.className = i < 52 ? "lb" : i < 61 ? "task" : "rest";
    waffle.appendChild(cell);
  }

  // Stack machine
  var PROGRAM = [
    { say: "PUSH 5 puts the number 5 on top of the stack.", run: function (s) { s.push(5); } },
    { say: "PUSH 7 puts 7 on top of it.", run: function (s) { s.push(7); } },
    { say: "ADD takes the top two numbers off and puts their sum back: 12.", run: function (s) { s.push(s.pop() + s.pop()); } }
  ];
  var stack = [];
  var pc = 0;
  var codeItems = document.querySelectorAll("#vm-code li");
  var stackHost = document.getElementById("vm-stack");
  var status = document.getElementById("vm-status");
  var stepButton = document.getElementById("vm-step");
  var resetButton = document.getElementById("vm-reset");

  function drawVm(message) {
    codeItems.forEach(function (li, index) {
      li.className = index < pc ? "done" : index === pc ? "next" : "";
    });
    stackHost.textContent = "";
    if (!stack.length) {
      var empty = document.createElement("em");
      empty.textContent = "empty";
      stackHost.appendChild(empty);
    }
    stack.forEach(function (value) {
      var slot = document.createElement("span");
      slot.textContent = value;
      stackHost.appendChild(slot);
    });
    status.textContent = message;
    stepButton.disabled = pc >= PROGRAM.length;
    resetButton.disabled = pc === 0;
  }
  stepButton.addEventListener("click", function () {
    var step = PROGRAM[pc];
    step.run(stack);
    pc += 1;
    drawVm(step.say + (pc >= PROGRAM.length ? " The program is finished." : ""));
  });
  resetButton.addEventListener("click", function () {
    stack = [];
    pc = 0;
    drawVm("Press Step to run the first instruction.");
  });
  drawVm("Press Step to run the first instruction.");

  // Millisecond ruler: the frame spans the full width, with one tick per whole millisecond.
  var fps = document.getElementById("fps");
  var ruler = document.getElementById("ruler");
  var readout = document.getElementById("clock-readout");
  var presets = Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll(".presets button"));
  function drawClock() {
    var rate = Number(fps.value);
    var frame = 1000 / rate;
    var whole = Math.floor(frame + 1e-9);
    document.getElementById("fps-out").textContent = rate;
    presets.forEach(function (b) { b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(Number(b.dataset.fps) === rate)); });
    ruler.textContent = "";
    // Label only as many ticks as fit: about 56 pixels per label.
    var width = ruler.clientWidth || 600;
    var need = 56 / (width / frame);
    var every = need <= 1 ? 1 : need <= 2 ? 2 : need <= 5 ? 5 : 10;
    for (var ms = 1; ms <= whole; ms++) {
      if (ms / frame > 0.999) break;
      var tick = document.createElement("span");
      tick.className = "tick";
      tick.style.left = (ms / frame * 100) + "%";
      if (ms % every === 0 && (1 - ms / frame) * width > 50) {
        var label = document.createElement("b");
        label.textContent = ms + " ms";
        tick.appendChild(label);
      }
      ruler.appendChild(tick);
    }
    var rest = frame - whole;
    var hasRest = rest > 0.005;
    if (hasRest) {
      var leftover = document.createElement("span");
      leftover.className = "leftover";
      leftover.style.width = (rest / frame * 100) + "%";
      ruler.insertBefore(leftover, ruler.firstChild);
    }
    document.getElementById("ruler-key").hidden = !hasRest;
    var share = 100 / frame;
    readout.textContent = "";
    var lead = document.createElement("strong");
    lead.textContent = "One frame lasts " + frame.toFixed(2) + " ms. ";
    readout.appendChild(lead);
    var percent = (share < 10 ? share.toFixed(1) : share.toFixed(0)) + "% of this frame.";
    readout.appendChild(document.createTextNode(hasRest
      ? "A clock that counts whole milliseconds sees " + whole + " or " + (whole + 1) + ", never " + frame.toFixed(2) + ". Any reading can be off by up to 1 ms, which is " + percent
      : "A clock that counts whole milliseconds sees " + whole + " only when frames are perfectly steady. Real frames vary, and any reading can be off by up to 1 ms, which is " + percent));
  }
  fps.addEventListener("input", drawClock);
  window.addEventListener("resize", drawClock);
  presets.forEach(function (button) {
    button.addEventListener("click", function () { fps.value = button.dataset.fps; drawClock(); });
  });
  drawClock();
})();
```

```html
    <h1>LibertyFlux</h1>
    <p class="lede">Grand Theft Auto IV's engine, being rewritten in Rust by AI agents one function at a time, so the game can eventually run as a native 64-bit program on Windows, Windows on ARM and macOS.</p>
    <p class="status-line" id="status-line">Phase 0 of 7: measuring the executable. Nothing is rewritten yet and the game is not playable.</p>

    <figure class="map-figure">

  <section id="progress" class="band">
    <div class="wrap">
      <h2>Progress</h2>
      <p class="prose" id="progress-empty" hidden></p>
      <ul class="meters" id="meters"></ul>

  <section id="how">
    <div class="wrap">
      <h2>How it works, step by step</h2>
      <p class="prose">AI agents do the rewriting. A machine check, not an agent's opinion, decides when a function is finished.</p>
      <ol class="steps">
        <li><div><h3>Measure the executable</h3><p>Ghidra, a reverse-engineering tool, analyses the original program. Functions are counted, the compiler's own runtime and third-party library code is set aside, and class names are recovered from the type information the compiler left behind.</p></div></li>
        <li><div><h3>Queue the work</h3><p>A script orders the functions from easiest to hardest and hands them out one at a time. Agents never choose their own.</p></div></li>
        <li><div><h3>Rewrite in Rust</h3><p>An agent studies what the function does, with the most similar finished functions as reference, and writes a Rust implementation.</p></div></li>
        <li><div><h3>Compare against the original</h3><p>The original function and the Rust version are run side by side in a small 32-bit test process, from the same inputs and the same starting memory. If their results, memory writes and outgoing calls agree, the function is accepted. If not, the agent tries again or hands it on.</p></div></li>
        <li><div><h3>Swap it into the running game</h3><p>Accepted functions are loaded into the original game, each with its own on/off switch. If the game misbehaves, switches are flipped in halves until the faulty function is found.</p></div></li>
        <li><div><h3>Cut the original loose</h3><p>When every function has a Rust replacement, the Rust code is built on its own, made 64-bit, and given a new renderer.</p></div></li>
      </ol>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section id="rule">
    <div class="wrap">
      <h2>What is in the repository, and what never is</h2>
      <div class="rule-grid">
        <div class="allowed">
          <h3>Committed</h3>
          <ul>
            <li>Structures: fields, sizes, offsets, enums, virtual table order</li>
            <li>Symbols: names, addresses, signatures, hashes, class hierarchy</li>
            <li>Rust rewrites of the engine's behaviour</li>
            <li>Tooling, tests and documentation</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
        <div class="never">
          <h3>Never committed</h3>
          <ul>
            <li>Decompiler output or disassembly, edited or not</li>
            <li>C or C++ reconstructions of original functions</li>
            <li>Code copied from other reverse-engineering projects</li>
            <li>Game executables, data or assets</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </div>
      <h3 class="after-grid">Buy the game</h3>
      <p class="prose">LibertyFlux is not a way to get Grand Theft Auto IV for free, and it never will be. Nothing here contains the game. To use it you need a copy that you paid for: buy it on <a href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/12210/">Steam</a>, from an authorised key seller, or from a retailer.</p>
      <p class="prose">Pirated and cracked copies are not supported. This project will never distribute game files, keys, cracks or ways around the game's copy protection. The people who made the game should be paid for it.</p>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section id="possible">
    <div class="wrap">
      <h2>What the rewrite makes possible</h2>
      <p class="note">None of this exists yet. These are the reasons for doing the work, and each depends on the phases above it in the roadmap. The pictures are concept images made for this page, not screenshots.</p>

      <ul class="features">
        <li class="feature">
          <figure><img src="img/high-frame-rate.webp" width="1600" height="900" loading="lazy" alt="Concept painting of a car crossing a suspension bridge at dusk, the bridge streaking past."><figcaption>Concept image, not a screenshot.</figcaption></figure>
          <div>
            <h3>Hundreds of frames per second</h3>
            <p>The original ties parts of its physics, animation and scripting to the frame rate, which is why it misbehaves above 60. The rewrite runs the simulation at a fixed rate and draws as fast as the hardware allows.</p>
            <p class="when">Planned for phase 6.</p>
          </div>
        </li>
        <li class="feature">
          <figure><img src="img/upscaling.webp" width="1600" height="900" loading="lazy" alt="Concept painting of a row of brownstone buildings, coarse and blocky on the left and resolving to fine detail on the right."><figcaption>Concept image, not a screenshot.</figcaption></figure>
          <div>
            <h3>Modern upscaling and frame generation</h3>
            <p>DLSS, FSR, XeSS and MetalFX behind one setting. The new renderer is designed from the start to produce the motion and depth information these need, which the original never did.</p>
            <p class="when">Planned for phase 7.</p>
          </div>
        </li>
        <li class="feature">
          <figure><img src="img/path-tracing.webp" width="1600" height="900" loading="lazy" alt="Concept painting of a rain-soaked street at night with streetlights reflected in puddles."><figcaption>Concept image, not a screenshot.</figcaption></figure>
          <div>
            <h3>Path tracing</h3>
            <p>Light that bounces, reflects and casts soft shadows the way it does outdoors, in a city made of wet streets, brick and sodium lamps.</p>
            <p class="when">A stretch goal, after the new renderer exists.</p>
          </div>
        </li>
        <li class="feature">
          <figure><img src="img/platforms.webp" width="1600" height="900" loading="lazy" alt="Concept painting of a desk with a monitor and two laptops showing the same city skyline."><figcaption>Concept image, not a screenshot.</figcaption></figure>
          <div>
            <h3>Native on three platforms</h3>
            <p>64-bit Windows, Windows on ARM and macOS on Apple silicon, each as a native build with no emulation layer in between.</p>
            <p class="when">Planned for phases 5 and 6.</p>
          </div>
        </li>
        <li class="feature">
          <figure><img src="img/new-gameplay.webp" width="1600" height="900" loading="lazy" alt="Concept painting of a busy city intersection seen from a rooftop."><figcaption>Concept image, not a screenshot.</figcaption></figure>
          <div>
            <h3>New gameplay and graphics</h3>
            <p>Once the engine is Rust that this project wrote, any part of it can change: new mechanics, denser streets, longer draw distances, and mods that reach parts of the engine no script hook can.</p>
            <p class="when">Planned for phase 7.</p>
          </div>
        </li>
      </ul>

      <ul class="plain-features">
        <li><strong>Nothing extra to install.</strong> No .NET, no launcher, no Visual C++ or DirectX runtime packages.</li>
        <li><strong>The game you already own.</strong> It uses the data files from your own copy and ships none of them.</li>
        <li><strong>Old bugs become tests.</strong> The community's list of high-frame-rate bugs is the checklist the new simulation has to pass.</li>
      </ul>

      <h3 class="after-grid">Planned platforms</h3>
      <table role="table">
        <thead role="rowgroup"><tr role="row"><th role="columnheader" scope="col">Platform</th><th role="columnheader" scope="col">Graphics</th><th role="columnheader" scope="col">Upscaling</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody role="rowgroup">
          <tr role="row"><td role="cell">Windows x64</td><td role="cell" data-label="Graphics">Vulkan, with Direct3D 12 optional</td><td role="cell" data-label="Upscaling">DLSS, FSR, XeSS</td></tr>
          <tr role="row"><td role="cell">Windows on ARM</td><td role="cell" data-label="Graphics">Vulkan</td><td role="cell" data-label="Upscaling">FSR</td></tr>
          <tr role="row"><td role="cell">macOS on Apple silicon</td><td role="cell" data-label="Graphics">MoltenVK, then native Metal</td><td role="cell" data-label="Upscaling">MetalFX</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section id="credits">
    <div class="wrap">
      <h2>Projects this builds on</h2>
      <p class="prose">The method is borrowed. These projects were studied for how they work, not for their code.</p>
      <ul class="sources">
        <li><a href="https://github.com/Veradictus/Thief3-Decomp">Thief 3 decompilation</a>: the work queue, attempt limits, and the rule that workers can only write to scratch space.</li>
        <li><a href="https://github.com/gta-reversed/gta-reversed">gta-reversed</a>: replacing functions inside the running game with a switch for each, and compile-time checks on structure sizes.</li>
        <li><a href="https://github.com/cdlewis/snowboardkids2-decomp">Snowboard Kids 2 decompilation</a>: letting a script pick the next function, and showing agents similar finished work.</li>
        <li><a href="https://github.com/OZORDI/LibertyRecomp">LibertyRecomp</a>: written-up engine internals from the Xbox 360 version, and what a renderer must supply for modern upscalers.</li>
        <li><a href="https://github.com/ShinyWasabi/scrDbg">scrDbg</a>: the script engine's layout on the current Steam build.</li>
        <li><a href="https://github.com/Zolika1351/iv-sdk">IV-SDK</a> and <a href="https://github.com/ThirteenAG/GTAIV.EFLC.FusionFix">FusionFix</a>: years of community knowledge about the game's classes and its frame-rate bugs.</li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="closing" id="pitch">
    <img src="img/closing.webp" width="1600" height="900" loading="lazy" alt="">
    <div class="wrap">
      <h2>Liberty City deserves a better program around it</h2>
      <p>The city, the writing and the physics still hold up. The 2008 PC port around them does not: it is 32-bit, it renders on one thread, and its simulation changes with the frame rate.</p>
      <p>LibertyFlux replaces that program one function at a time, checks each replacement against the original, and keeps the game playing exactly as it did. When the last function is done, everything on this page becomes buildable.</p>
      <div class="actions">
        <a class="primary" href="#roadmap">See the roadmap</a>
        <a href="#how">See how each function is checked</a>
      </div>
      <p class="closing-credit">Background: concept image, not a screenshot.</p>
    </div>
  </section>
```

`docs/site.js`:

```js
function render(data) {
  var stages = data.stages || {};
  var functions = data.functions || {};
  var total = functions.game;
  var fmt = new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US");

  var STAGE_NAMES = {
    unmeasured: "Not measured",
    identified: "Identified",
    named: "Named",
    rewritten: "Rewritten in Rust",
    verified: "Verified"
  };

  var PHASES = [
    ["Measure", "measuring the executable", "Analyse the executable, count its functions, set library code aside, recover class names.", "The function count and class list exist."],
    ["Harness", "building the harness", "Build the work queue, the side-by-side comparison, and the loader that swaps functions into the game.", "50 functions pass the comparison and run in the game."],
    ["Pilot", "running the pilot", "Run a few agents for several days. Measure how many functions pass, and how many passed wrongly.", "A measured rate replaces the estimate."],
    ["Rewrite", "rewriting functions", "Scale up the agents and rewrite every game function in Rust.", "The game plays with every replacement switched on."],
    ["Standalone", "building the standalone game", "Build the Rust code as its own 32-bit program.", "It runs without the original executable."],
    ["64-bit", "moving to 64-bit", "Convert the game's 32-bit data files as they load, and replace every Windows-only call.", "Windows x64 and Windows on ARM builds play."],
    ["Renderer", "building the renderer", "Write a Vulkan renderer, run the simulation at a fixed rate, and bring up macOS.", "Frame rate is measured on all three platforms."],
    ["Upscalers and new work", "adding upscalers and new work", "Add DLSS, FSR, XeSS and MetalFX, then new gameplay, graphics and path tracing.", "Each upscaler is verified on hardware that supports it."]
  ];

  function el(tag, className, text) {
    var node = document.createElement(tag);
    if (className) node.className = className;
    if (text != null) node.textContent = text;
    return node;
  }

  function prettyDate(iso) {
    var d = new Date(iso + "T00:00:00Z");
    if (isNaN(d)) return null;
    return d.toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "short", year: "numeric", timeZone: "UTC" });
  }

  // Status line
  var current = data.phase ? data.phase.index : 0;
  var statusLine = document.getElementById("status-line");
  statusLine.replaceChildren();
  statusLine.appendChild(el("strong", null, "Phase " + current + " of " + (PHASES.length - 1) + ": " + PHASES[current][1] + "."));
  var done = stages.rewritten || 0;
  var summary = done
    ? " " + fmt.format(done) + " functions rewritten, " + fmt.format(stages.verified || 0) + " verified."
    : " Nothing is rewritten yet.";
  if (current < 4) summary += " The game is not playable.";
  var when = data.updated ? prettyDate(data.updated) : null;
  if (when) summary += " Updated " + when + ".";
  statusLine.appendChild(document.createTextNode(summary));

  // Code map
  var mapEl = document.getElementById("map");
  var emptyEl = document.getElementById("map-empty");
  var legendEl = document.getElementById("legend");
  var readout = document.getElementById("map-readout");
  var tip = document.getElementById("tip");
  var cells = Array.isArray(data.map) && data.map.length ? data.map : null;

  if (!cells) {
    emptyEl.hidden = false;
  } else {
    mapEl.hidden = false;
    legendEl.hidden = false;
    var perCell = total ? Math.round(total / cells.length) : null;
    var title = document.getElementById("map-title");
    title.appendChild(document.createTextNode(
      " Each square is " + (perCell ? "about " + fmt.format(perCell) + " functions" : "a slice of the code") +
      " in address order, left to right and top to bottom, and shows its least-advanced function."));

    var defaultReadout = data.mapRange || "";
    readout.textContent = defaultReadout;

    var nodes = cells.map(function (entry) {
      var cell = el("span", "cell");
      var stage = STAGE_NAMES[entry.stage] ? entry.stage : "unmeasured";
      cell.dataset.stage = stage;
      cell.dataset.range = entry.from + " to " + entry.to;
      cell.dataset.detail = STAGE_NAMES[stage] + (entry.count ? ", " + fmt.format(entry.count) + " functions" : "");
      mapEl.appendChild(cell);
      return cell;
    });

    mapEl.tabIndex = 0;
    mapEl.setAttribute("role", "group");
    mapEl.setAttribute("aria-label",
      "Map of the game's code. " +
      (total ? fmt.format(stages.identified || 0) + " of " + fmt.format(total) + " functions identified, " +
        fmt.format(stages.rewritten || 0) + " rewritten, " + fmt.format(stages.verified || 0) + " verified. " : "") +
      "Use the arrow keys to inspect a square.");

    var active = -1;
    function select(index) {
      if (active >= 0) nodes[active].classList.remove("active");
      active = index;
      if (index < 0) { readout.textContent = defaultReadout; return; }
      var node = nodes[index];
      node.classList.add("active");
      readout.textContent = node.dataset.range + ": " + node.dataset.detail;
    }
    function columns() {
      return getComputedStyle(mapEl).gridTemplateColumns.split(" ").length;
    }

    mapEl.addEventListener("keydown", function (e) {
      var step = { ArrowRight: 1, ArrowLeft: -1, ArrowDown: columns(), ArrowUp: -columns() }[e.key];
      if (!step) return;
      e.preventDefault();
      var next = active < 0 ? 0 : active + step;
      if (next >= 0 && next < nodes.length) select(next);
    });
    mapEl.addEventListener("blur", function () { select(-1); });
    mapEl.addEventListener("click", function (e) {
      var index = nodes.indexOf(e.target);
      if (index >= 0) select(index);
    });

    mapEl.addEventListener("mousemove", function (e) {
      var index = nodes.indexOf(e.target);
      if (index < 0) return; // over a gap: keep the last square's tooltip, no flicker
      var node = nodes[index];
      tip.replaceChildren(el("span", "addr", node.dataset.range), document.createElement("br"), document.createTextNode(node.dataset.detail));
      tip.style.left = Math.min(e.clientX + 14, window.innerWidth - tip.offsetWidth - 8) + "px";
      tip.style.top = (e.clientY + 16) + "px";
      tip.classList.add("on");
    });
    mapEl.addEventListener("mouseleave", function () { tip.classList.remove("on"); });
  }

  // What has been measured so far, and how much work is in flight. Shown until functions are counted.
  function renderMeasured(after) {
    var facts = Array.isArray(data.measured) ? data.measured : [];
    var activity = data.activity;
    if (!facts.length && !activity) return;
    var wrap = el("div", "measured");
    if (activity) {
      var line = "Right now: " + fmt.format(activity.lanes_running || 0) + " agent lanes running, " +
        fmt.format(activity.lanes_finished || 0) + " finished, " +
        fmt.format(activity.devlog_entries || 0) + " devlog entries written.";
      if (data.updated_at) line += " As of " + data.updated_at + ".";
      wrap.appendChild(el("p", "prose", line));
    }
    if (facts.length) {
      wrap.appendChild(el("h3", null, "Measured so far"));
      var list = el("ul", "facts");
      facts.forEach(function (fact) {
        var li = el("li");
        li.appendChild(document.createTextNode(fact.label + ": "));
        li.appendChild(el("strong", null, fmt.format(fact.value)));
        if (fact.unit) li.appendChild(document.createTextNode(" " + fact.unit));
        list.appendChild(li);
      });
      wrap.appendChild(list);
    }
    after.insertAdjacentElement("afterend", wrap);
  }

  // Meters
  var metersEl = document.getElementById("meters");
  var note = document.getElementById("meter-note");
  if (!total) {
    var empty = document.getElementById("progress-empty");
    empty.hidden = false;
    empty.textContent = "No functions have been counted yet, so there is nothing to chart. For scale: the LibertyRecomp and GTA-IV-RECOMP projects count between about 31,800 and 36,400 functions in the Xbox 360 version of the same game. The PC version should be similar.";
    metersEl.hidden = true;
    note.hidden = true;
    renderMeasured(empty);
  } else {
    ["identified", "named", "rewritten", "verified"].forEach(function (key) {
      var count = stages[key] || 0;
      var pct = Math.min(100, (count / total) * 100);
      var li = el("li", "meter-row");
      li.appendChild(el("span", "meter-label", STAGE_NAMES[key]));
      li.appendChild(el("span", "meter-value", fmt.format(count) + " of " + fmt.format(total) + " (" + pct.toFixed(1) + "%)"));
      var track = el("div", "meter-track");
      track.setAttribute("role", "progressbar");
      track.setAttribute("aria-label", STAGE_NAMES[key]);
      track.setAttribute("aria-valuemin", "0");
      track.setAttribute("aria-valuemax", "100");
      track.setAttribute("aria-valuenow", pct.toFixed(1));
      var fill = el("div", "meter-fill");
      fill.style.width = pct + "%";
      track.appendChild(fill);
      li.appendChild(track);
      metersEl.appendChild(li);
    });
    note.textContent =
      "Each stage includes the ones after it. Identified: the function's start and end are known. Named: it has a meaningful name. " +
      "Rewritten: it has a Rust implementation. Verified: the comparison against the original passed. " +
      fmt.format(data.structures || 0) + " structures and " + fmt.format(data.symbols || 0) + " symbols are documented. " +
      "The compiler's runtime and third-party library code (" + fmt.format(functions.library || 0) + " functions) is not counted.";
  }

  // Roadmap
  var body = document.getElementById("roadmap-body");
  PHASES.forEach(function (p, idx) {
    var tr = document.createElement("tr");
    tr.setAttribute("role", "row");
    tr.className = idx < current ? "done" : idx === current ? "current" : "todo";
    var name = el("td");
    name.appendChild(el("span", "phase-num", String(idx)));
    name.appendChild(document.createTextNode(" " + p[0]));
    var work = el("td", null, p[2]);
    var gate = el("td", null, p[3]);
    var status = el("td", "status", idx < current ? "Done" : idx === current ? "In progress" : "Not started");
    gate.dataset.label = "Finished when";
    status.dataset.label = "Status";
    [name, work, gate, status].forEach(function (td) { td.setAttribute("role", "cell"); tr.appendChild(td); });
    body.appendChild(tr);
  });
}

// The page's numbers come straight from data/progress.json.
fetch("data/progress.json", { cache: "no-store" })
  .then(function (response) { return response.ok ? response.json() : {}; })
  .catch(function () { return {}; })
  .then(render);

```

`documentation/upscaling-and-frame-generation.md`:

```md
# Upscaling, frame generation and ray-tracing denoising: reference

This document surveys the current upscaling, frame generation and ray-tracing denoising frameworks from NVIDIA, AMD, Intel and Apple for a new Rust Vulkan renderer targeting Windows x64, Windows on ARM64 and macOS on Apple silicon. It was researched on 2026-10-03 from vendor documentation, vendor repositories and integration guides. Every factual claim carries a link to its source: `(verified)` means the linked page was opened and read, `(inferred)` means the claim comes from a search snippet, summary or unread portion of a source.

## Summary table

| Framework | Parts | APIs | Platforms | Hardware | Licence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [DLSS](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss) (verified) | [SR, FG, MFG, RR, DLAA, Reflex](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss) (verified) | [DX11, DX12, Vulkan](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/blob/main/doc/DLSS_Programming_Guide_Release.pdf) (inferred) | [x64 yes](https://github.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/releases/expanded_assets/v2.14.1) (verified); [ARM64 no](https://videocardz.com/newz/nvidia-rtx-neural-texture-compression-adds-windows-arm64-support-for-rtx-spark) (inferred); macOS no (inferred) | [RTX GPU only](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss) (verified) | [NVIDIA RTX SDK licence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/main/LICENSE.txt) (verified) |
| [FSR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/readme.md) (verified) | [Upscale 2/3/4, FG 3/4, RR, RC](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/readme.md) (verified) | [DX12, Vulkan](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/readme.md) (verified) | x64 yes (verified); ARM64 partial (inferred); macOS unconfirmed | [Most GPUs; ML parts RDNA3/4](https://github.com/shooterspps/OptiScaler) (inferred) | Source MIT (inferred); ML DLLs signed (verified) |
| [XeSS](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/README.md) (verified) | [SR, FG, low latency](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/README.md) (verified) | [SR: DX11/12, Vulkan; FG: DX12](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_fg_developer_guide_english.md) (verified) | [x64 yes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_fg_developer_guide_english.md) (verified); ARM64 no (inferred); macOS no (inferred) | [SM 6.4 DP4a; Arc preferred](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/README.md) (verified) | [Intel simplified licence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/LICENSE.txt) (verified) |
| [MetalFX](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metalfx) (verified) | [Spatial, temporal, interp, denoise](https://developer.apple.com/metal/sample-code/) (inferred) | [Metal only](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metalfx) (inferred) | Win no; macOS Apple silicon yes (inferred) | [M1 or later](https://www.tweaktown.com/news/86706/metalfx-upscaling-apples-take-on-nvidia-dlss-amd-fsr-intel-xess/index.html) (inferred) | Apple SDK terms; ships with OS (inferred) |

## What the renderer must provide

All four temporal upscalers need the same class of per-frame data, though exact conventions differ per vendor:

- A low-resolution jittered HDR colour buffer rendered before most post-processing. XeSS-SR is documented as compute passes [executed before the post-processing stage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_sr_developer_guide_english.md) (verified), DLSS takes the [raw colour buffer in HDR or LDR space](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/blob/main/doc/DLSS_Programming_Guide_Release.pdf) (inferred), and FSR requires input colour in [linear colourspace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-ml.md) (verified).
- A depth buffer for the frame. DLSS requires [the depth buffer each evaluate call](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/blob/main/doc/DLSS_Programming_Guide_Release.pdf) (inferred); FSR, XeSS and MetalFX temporal paths all document depth inputs ([FSR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-upscaler.md) (verified), [XeSS](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_sr_developer_guide_english.md) (verified), [MetalFX](https://github.com/theapplaunchers/apple-docs-for-rag/blob/HEAD/WWDC2025/api/MetalFX.md) (inferred)).
- Per-pixel motion vectors updated every frame. DLSS requires [screen-space motion vectors at 16 or 32 bits per pixel, updated each frame](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/blob/main/doc/DLSS_Programming_Guide_Release.pdf) (inferred); the other three document motion vector inputs with unread conventions (see differences table).
- A subpixel camera jitter sequence applied to the projection matrix. DLSS requires [subpixel viewport jitter with at least 16 phases, 32 or more preferred](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/blob/main/doc/DLSS_Programming_Guide_Release.pdf) (inferred); FSR, XeSS and MetalFX document their own jitter sections ([FSR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-upscaler.md) (verified), [XeSS](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_sr_developer_guide_english.md) (verified), [MetalFX sample](https://developer.apple.com/metal/sample-code/) (inferred)).
- Exposure or pre-exposure values when rendering in HDR. DLSS exposes [preExposure and exposureScale options](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/main/include/sl_dlss.h) (verified); FSR and XeSS document [exposure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-upscaler.md) (verified) and [exposure multiplier](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_sr_developer_guide_english.md) (verified) inputs.
- A reset or invalidation signal on camera cuts and resolution changes. FSR documents [camera jump cuts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-upscaler.md) (verified); equivalent handling for the others is unconfirmed from the sources read.
- For frame generation: HUD-less colour plus separate UI, and a vendor-owned or vendor-driven swap chain. XeSS-FG documents [HUD-less colour, UI texture and UI composition modes with a proxy swap chain](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_fg_developer_guide_english.md) (verified); FSR frame generation ships a [replacement DXGI swap chain for DX12](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/readme.md) (verified); DLSS frame generation routes presentation through [Streamline's DLSS-G proxy swap chain](https://github.com/thierbig/bg3fgvk/blob/HEAD/docs/2026-08-27-fgvk-design.md) (inferred).
- Mipmap biasing for sampled textures under upscaling. FSR and XeSS both document [mipmap biasing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-upscaler.md) (verified) ([mip bias](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_sr_developer_guide_english.md) (verified)); DLSS and MetalFX equivalents are unconfirmed.
- Replacement of the built-in TAA pass, since temporal upscalers supersede it. Godot uses [FSR2 at scale 1.0 as a TAA solution](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_viewport.html) (inferred); FSR documents a [temporal antialiasing section](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-upscaler.md) (verified).

Where the frameworks differ:

| Framework | Motion vectors | Depth | Jitter | Masks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DLSS | [Screen-space 16/32-bit](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/blob/main/doc/DLSS_Programming_Guide_Release.pdf) (inferred); sign and units unconfirmed | [Per-frame depth](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/blob/main/doc/DLSS_Programming_Guide_Release.pdf) (inferred); convention unconfirmed | [16+ phases, 32+ preferred](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/blob/main/doc/DLSS_Programming_Guide_Release.pdf) (inferred) | Extra mask inputs unconfirmed |
| FSR | [Section exists, body unread](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-upscaler.md) (verified) | [Configs section exists](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-upscaler.md) (verified) | [Section exists, body unread](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-upscaler.md) (verified) | [Reactive, transparency, composition](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-upscaler.md) (verified) |
| XeSS | [MV plus velocity scale](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_sr_developer_guide_english.md) (verified); convention unread | [Depth section exists](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_sr_developer_guide_english.md) (verified) | [Sequence section exists](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_sr_developer_guide_english.md) (verified) | [Responsive pixel mask](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_sr_developer_guide_english.md) (verified) |
| MetalFX | [Motion vector texture](https://developer.apple.com/metal/sample-code/) (inferred) | Depth input (inferred) | [Jitter during render](https://developer.apple.com/metal/sample-code/) (inferred) | Mask types unconfirmed |

## NVIDIA DLSS

### Components and current version

- DLSS Super Resolution outputs higher-resolution frames from lower-resolution input using multiple prior frames, motion data and a transformer model ([source](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss) (verified)).
- DLSS Frame Generation generates interpolated frames, and Multi Frame Generation generates [up to five frames per rendered frame on GeForce RTX 50 series and RTX PRO Blackwell GPUs with fifth-generation Tensor Cores](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss) (verified).
- Dynamic Multi Frame Generation [dynamically adjusts the generation multiplier](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss) (verified) and is part of DLSS 4.5 with a second-generation transformer model ([source](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss) (verified)); DLSS 4 introduced MFG and the first transformer model ([source](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss) (verified)).
- DLSS Ray Reconstruction [replaces hand-tuned denoisers with an AI network that generates pixels between sampled rays](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss) (verified).
- DLAA applies [the same Super Resolution technology at native resolution as AI anti-aliasing](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss) (verified), and appears as a mode alongside the upscaling modes in the Streamline header ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/main/include/sl_dlss.h) (verified)).
- NVIDIA Reflex is the latency-reduction companion linked from the DLSS page ([source](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss) (verified)); Reflex is [required for DLSS Frame Generation and turns on automatically with it](https://github.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/raw/refs/heads/main/docs/RTX%20UI%20Developer%20Guidelines.pdf?download=) (inferred).
- The current DLSS SDK is [version 310.9.1, published 2026-09-08](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/releases/expanded_assets/v310.9.1) (verified), and the current Streamline SDK is [version 2.14.1, published 2026-09-08](https://github.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/releases/expanded_assets/v2.14.1) (verified).
- DLSS 5 exists: NVIDIA's September 2026 developer blog describes [DLSS 5 with 3D-guided neural rendering](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/whats-new-for-game-developers-dlss-5-with-3d-guided-neural-rendering-nvidia-ace-updates-and-new-rtx-kit-capabilities/) (verified), operating [one frame in, one frame out on engine motion vectors, locally on RTX 50 series GPUs at up to 4K](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/whats-new-for-game-developers-dlss-5-with-3d-guided-neural-rendering-nvidia-ace-updates-and-new-rtx-kit-capabilities/) (verified), with [model selection, structure and tone intensity controls and semantic masking](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/whats-new-for-game-developers-dlss-5-with-3d-guided-neural-rendering-nvidia-ace-updates-and-new-rtx-kit-capabilities/) (verified). It reportedly [launched 2026-09-03 with NBA 2K27 as the first title](https://tech-insider.org/nvidia-dlss-5-siggraph-2026/) (inferred), and an [RTX 40 update with a reduced feature set was reported](https://tech-insider.org/nvidia-dlss-5-rtx-40-gpus-no-full-control-2026/) (inferred). The developer DLSS page read for this research describes up to DLSS 4.5 and does not mention DLSS 5 ([source](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss) (verified)), so SDK availability of the neural rendering runtime is unconfirmed.

### Platforms and requirements

- DLSS Super Resolution supports [DirectX 11, DirectX 12 and Vulkan, with Vulkan 1.1 or later](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/blob/main/doc/DLSS_Programming_Guide_Release.pdf) (inferred).
- DLSS Frame Generation supports [DirectX 12 and Vulkan through Streamline](https://github.com/silynometa/dlssg_for_sm86/blob/HEAD/docs/INSTALL.en.md) (inferred); driver-based Smooth Motion frame generation supports [Vulkan on RTX 50 x86-64](https://www.khronos.org/news/permalink/nvidia-adds-vulkan-support-to-smooth-motion-frame-generation-a-boost-for-many-games-and-emulators) (inferred).
- Streamline requires [Windows 10 20H1 or newer, NVIDIA driver 512.15 or newer, and a GPU with DirectX 11 and Vulkan 1.2 or higher](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/main/README.md) (verified).
- Linux is supported at least for the DLSS sample: the SDK release ships [separate Windows and Linux demo archives](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/releases/expanded_assets/v310.9.1) (verified).
- Windows x64 is supported ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/releases/expanded_assets/v2.14.1) (verified)). Windows on ARM64: Streamline ships [aarch64 and arm64ec SDK archives](https://github.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/releases/expanded_assets/v2.14.1) (verified) and builds for [amd64, arm64 and arm64ec](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/main/README.md) (verified), but DLSS itself is [reported as not supported on Windows ARM64](https://videocardz.com/newz/nvidia-rtx-neural-texture-compression-adds-windows-arm64-support-for-rtx-spark) (inferred), so the ARM64 archives presumably cover the framework and non-DLSS plugins; this division is unconfirmed from a primary source.
- All DLSS components require [NVIDIA RTX GPUs with Tensor Cores](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss) (verified); MFG additionally requires RTX 50 series or Blackwell ([source](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss) (verified)); plain frame generation is [reported to require RTX 40 series or newer](https://github.com/noplace/psxemu/blob/HEAD/Docs/DLSS-Plan.md) (inferred). No macOS support was found in the sources read (inferred).

### Inputs

- Each DLSS-SR evaluate call takes [raw HDR or LDR colour, screen-space motion vectors, depth and an exposure value](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/blob/main/doc/DLSS_Programming_Guide_Release.pdf) (inferred).
- Jitter must be [subpixel viewport jitter with at least 16 phases, 32 or more preferred](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/blob/main/doc/DLSS_Programming_Guide_Release.pdf) (inferred).
- The Streamline DLSS options struct carries [mode, output width and height, pre-exposure, exposure scale, an HDR colour flag and per-mode presets](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/main/include/sl_dlss.h) (verified).
- Modes are [Off, MaxPerformance, Balanced, MaxQuality, UltraPerformance, UltraQuality and DLAA](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/main/include/sl_dlss.h) (verified); presets J and K are [transformer-based, with K the default quality choice](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/main/include/sl_dlss.h) (verified), while L and M are [defaults for UltraPerformance and Performance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/main/include/sl_dlss.h) (verified).
- Frame generation additionally needs [Reflex, a Streamline-owned swap chain, a HUD-less picture or UI mask, and hardware GPU scheduling](https://github.com/noplace/psxemu/blob/HEAD/Docs/DLSS-Plan.md) (inferred). Ray Reconstruction inputs are unconfirmed; only its [integration guide filename](https://api.github.com/repos/NVIDIA/DLSS/contents/doc) (verified) was confirmed.
- Resource formats, resolution limits and dynamic-resolution rules are unconfirmed from the sources read.

### Integration outline

1. Download a Streamline release archive, since [binaries are not in the repository and must come from the releases page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/main/README.md) (verified).
2. Integrate through Streamline rather than NGX, per NVIDIA's [get started with DLSS through Streamline](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss) (verified) guidance; Streamline provides [one integration for multiple vendors' super resolution](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/main/README.md) (verified). The older path is the [NGX interface](https://videocardz.com/newz/modder-gets-nvidia-dlss-working-in-a-web-browser) (inferred).
3. Configure the DLSS mode, output size, exposure values and presets via the documented options ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/main/include/sl_dlss.h) (verified)).
4. Supply colour, motion vectors, depth and exposure every frame, and drive the jitter sequence ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/blob/main/doc/DLSS_Programming_Guide_Release.pdf) (inferred)).
5. For frame generation, enable Reflex and hand presentation to the Streamline swap chain ([sources](https://github.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/raw/refs/heads/main/docs/RTX%20UI%20Developer%20Guidelines.pdf?download=) (inferred), ([source](https://github.com/thierbig/bg3fgvk/blob/HEAD/docs/2026-08-27-fgvk-design.md) (inferred)).
6. Ship [production builds with NVIDIA-signed DLLs or a custom signing check](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/main/README.md) (verified).

### Licence and redistribution

- The DLSS SDK is governed by the [NVIDIA RTX SDKs licence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/main/LICENSE.txt) (verified), which grants [installation and use, modification of sample source, and distribution of SDK software and materials in object form inside an application](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/main/LICENSE.txt) (verified).
- Redistribution requires [material additional functionality beyond the SDK portions, an NVIDIA source notice in derivatives, and downstream terms at least as protective](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/main/LICENSE.txt) (verified); the SDK [may not be distributed standalone or sublicensed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/main/LICENSE.txt) (verified), and [reverse engineering is prohibited](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/main/LICENSE.txt) (verified).
- An open-source game may therefore bundle the nvngx DLLs inside its own application distribution under those terms, but may not republish the SDK itself (verified from the licence terms above). Streamline headers are [MIT-style permissive](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/main/include/sl_dlss.h) (verified), while the DLSS-G plugin is [prebuilt DLLs only](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/main/README.md) (verified).

### Pitfalls

- Default presets [may change after an over-the-air update](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/main/include/sl_dlss.h) (verified), so pin presets deliberately.
- The in-header sharpening control is [deprecated and unsupported](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/main/include/sl_dlss.h) (verified).
- Only the DLSS-G plugin [cannot be rebuilt from source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/main/README.md) (verified); everything else in Streamline can be, though shipping the signed binaries is the norm ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/main/README.md) (verified)).
- Motion vectors must be [accurate and refreshed every frame](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/blob/main/doc/DLSS_Programming_Guide_Release.pdf) (inferred); Reflex [should be unavailable when a non-NVIDIA frame generation technology is active](https://github.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/raw/refs/heads/main/docs/RTX%20UI%20Developer%20Guidelines.pdf?download=) (inferred).

### Official documentation and guides

- [NVIDIA DLSS repository](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS) — SDK tree, sample sources and programming guides; page opened but largely truncated (verified).
- [NVIDIA DLSS developer page](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss) — component overview and Streamline entry point (verified).
- [Streamline repository](https://github.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline) — framework source, headers and release archives (verified).
- [Streamline 2.14.1 release assets](https://github.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/releases/expanded_assets/v2.14.1) — x64, aarch64 and arm64ec archives with hashes (verified).
- [DLSS 310.9.1 release assets](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/releases/expanded_assets/v310.9.1) — Windows and Linux demo archives (verified).
- [DLSS programming guide PDF](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/blob/main/doc/DLSS_Programming_Guide_Release.pdf) — per-frame requirements; listing confirmed, file not opened (link not opened).
- [DLSS frame generation and ray reconstruction guides](https://api.github.com/repos/NVIDIA/DLSS/contents/doc) — guide filenames and sizes in the repository listing (verified).
- [sl_dlss.h header](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/main/include/sl_dlss.h) — modes, presets and options (verified).
- [DLSS 5 developer blog](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/whats-new-for-game-developers-dlss-5-with-3d-guided-neural-rendering-nvidia-ace-updates-and-new-rtx-kit-capabilities/) — what DLSS 5 is and its controls (verified).
- [NVIDIA RTX Kit page](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx-kit) — neural rendering suite: neural shaders, texture compression, texture filtering, mega geometry and related SDKs (verified).

## AMD FSR

### Components and current version

- The current kit is the [AMD FSR SDK 2.3.0, codenamed Redstone, released 2026-06-24](https://api.github.com/repos/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/releases/latest) (verified), described in its own readme ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/readme.md) (verified)).
- Redstone is an [umbrella name for four machine-learning features: upscaling, frame generation, ray regeneration and radiance caching](https://tech-insider.org/amd-fsr-redstone-setup-2026/) (inferred).
- The SDK contains [FSR Temporal 2.3.4, FSR Upscaler 3.1.5, FSR ML upscaler 4.1.1, FSR Frame Generation 3.1.6, FSR FG SwapChain 3.1.7, FSR FG ML 4.0.1, FSR Ray Regeneration 1.2.0 and FSR Radiance Caching preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/readme.md) (verified).
- FSR 4 upscaling [uses machine learning over temporal and spatial information](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-ml.md) (verified) and requires [HLSL compute shader model 6.6](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-ml.md) (verified), while FSR 3.1 requires [CS 6.2, or 6.6 on 64-wide-wavefront hardware](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-upscaler.md) (verified).
- Both FSR 3.1 and FSR 4 expose [NativeAA 1.0x, Quality 1.5x, Balanced 1.7x, Performance 2.0x and Ultra Performance 3.0x presets](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-upscaler.md) (verified) ([FSR 4 source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-ml.md) (verified)).
- Ray Regeneration 1.2.0 added [ambient occlusion and specular occlusion denoising, checkerboard rendering support and new debug controls](https://api.github.com/repos/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/releases/latest) (verified), with [API-breaking struct changes](https://api.github.com/repos/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/releases/latest) (verified).
- Integration goes through the [FSR API of five functions: ffxCreateContext, ffxDestroyContext, ffxDispatch, ffxQuery and ffxConfigure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/getting-started/ffx-api.md) (verified), using [signed DLLs split per effect type since SDK 2.0](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/getting-started/ffx-api.md) (verified): loader, upscaler, frame generation, denoiser and radiance cache ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/getting-started/ffx-api.md) (verified)).

### Platforms and requirements

- The SDK targets [DirectX 12 or Vulkan applications](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/readme.md) (verified), and its samples run on [DirectX 12 and Vulkan](https://github.com/matheusgviana/dlss-5-amd-project/blob/HEAD/OptiScaler-DLSSNR-PreSR-Multipass-main/external/FidelityFX-SDK/docs/getting-started/index.md) (inferred).
- Backend-specific FSR API functionality is [currently only supported for DirectX 12](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/getting-started/ffx-api.md) (verified), and the ML SDK releases target [DirectX 12 on Windows 10 and 11](https://videocardz.com/newz/amd-launches-fsr-sdk-2-1-0-to-speed-up-adoption-of-fsr-redstone) (inferred), so Vulkan coverage of the ML components is unconfirmed.
- Windows x64 is supported ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/readme.md) (verified)). Windows on ARM64: FSR is [reported working on Snapdragon X Elite](https://www.pcgamer.com/hardware/gaming-laptops/qualcomms-new-windows-pc-chip-supports-amds-fsr-and-im-not-sure-amd-had-any-idea-about-it/) (inferred), but prebuilt FidelityFX libraries are [reported x86-64 only, needing a source rebuild for arm64ec](https://github.com/justradical/sloptiscaler/blob/HEAD/arm64ec/README.md) (inferred). macOS support is unconfirmed from the sources read.
- Analytical FSR 2/3 upscaling is vendor-agnostic, listed for [Radeon RX 500 series and above or equivalents](https://videocardz.com/newz/amd-releases-fsr-sdk-2-2-with-fsr-upscaling-4-1-and-fsr-ray-regeneration-1-1) (inferred), with frame generation 3.1.6 listed for [RX 5000 series and newer](https://videocardz.com/newz/amd-releases-fsr-sdk-2-2-with-fsr-upscaling-4-1-and-fsr-ray-regeneration-1-1) (inferred).
- FSR 4 ML upscaling officially supports [RDNA4 over FP8 and RDNA3 over INT8, with RDNA2 planned for 2027](https://github.com/characterecho-sean/edvr-unofficial-patch/blob/HEAD/docs/fsr-upscaler-design-2026-09-16.md) (inferred), falling back to [FSR 3.1.5 on other hardware](https://github.com/characterecho-sean/edvr-unofficial-patch/blob/HEAD/docs/fsr-upscaler-design-2026-09-16.md) (inferred).

### Inputs

- FSR upscaling takes [input colour, depth with several buffer configurations, motion vectors, a reactive mask, a transparency and composition mask, and exposure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-upscaler.md) (verified), plus [camera jitter, jump-cut handling, mipmap bias and frame time delta](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-upscaler.md) (verified). Exact vector, depth and jitter conventions sit in unread portions of that document and are unconfirmed.
- Input colour must be in [linear colourspace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-ml.md) (verified); otherwise the [FFX_UPSCALE_ENABLE_NON_LINEAR_COLORSPACE creation flag](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-ml.md) (verified) can be set with possible quality cost ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-ml.md) (verified)).
- Reactivity can be [generated automatically as well as supplied](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-upscaler.md) (verified).
- Frame generation consumes [multiple real frames and multiple motion vector sources](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/readme.md) (verified); its detailed inputs were not read and are unconfirmed.
- Placement relative to tone mapping and UI, formats and resolution limits sit in [documented but unread sections](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-upscaler.md) (verified) and are unconfirmed.

### Integration outline

1. Choose the analytical source path or the ML signed-binary path; FSR 4 [requires the FSR API and the signed binary distribution](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-ml.md) (verified).
2. Load the loader DLL at runtime and let it pull in only the effect DLLs used, since the split [lets applications ship only the effect types they use](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/getting-started/ffx-api.md) (verified); applications on the old combined DLL [must switch to the loader DLL](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/getting-started/ffx-api.md) (verified).
3. Drive effects through the five API functions with chained descriptor structs ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/getting-started/ffx-api.md) (verified)).
4. Supply colour, depth, motion vectors, masks and exposure, and implement jitter, cut handling, mip bias and frame delta ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-upscaler.md) (verified)).
5. For frame generation on DirectX 12, adopt the [replacement DXGI swap chain implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/readme.md) (verified); the Vulkan frame generation story is unconfirmed.
6. Validate with the SDK's upscaling, frame generation, denoiser and radiance cache samples ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/readme.md) (verified)).

### Licence and redistribution

- FSR 1 and FSR 2 source were released under the [MIT licence](https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2021/07/amd-releases-fidelityfx-super-resolution-source-code/) (inferred) ([FSR 2 source](https://www.techpowerup.com/296074/amd-releases-fsr-3-source-code-on-gpuopen?cp=1) (inferred)).
- No licence file was found at the repository root paths tried: both [license.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/license.txt) (verified 404) and [LICENSE.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/LICENSE.md) (verified 404) failed, so current SDK-wide terms are unconfirmed; a [third-party notice file exists at the root](https://api.github.com/repos/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/contents/) (verified).
- FSR API users [must use one of the provided signed DLLs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/getting-started/ffx-api.md) (verified), so redistribution of the ML stack means shipping AMD's signed binaries under terms that are unconfirmed here. Driver-based FSR upgrades may [update ML components in DX12 games without a game patch](https://videocardz.com/newz/amd-releases-fsr-sdk-2-2-with-fsr-upscaling-4-1-and-fsr-ray-regeneration-1-1) (inferred).

### Pitfalls

- Non-linear input colour without the compatibility flag degrades quality ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-ml.md) (verified)).
- Ray Regeneration 1.2.0 contains [API-breaking changes](https://api.github.com/repos/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/releases/latest) (verified); track the version history pages per effect.
- FSR 3.1 trades [slightly lower performance than 3.0 for higher quality](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-upscaler.md) (verified).
- Shading language level matters: [CS 6.6 on 64-wide hardware](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-upscaler.md) (verified) for FSR 3.1, CS 6.6 always for FSR 4 ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-ml.md) (verified)).
```
