```md
- [FSR API introduction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/getting-started/ffx-api.md) — five functions, descriptors and DLL split (verified).
- [FSR 3.1.5 upscaler guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-upscaler.md) — inputs, masks, jitter and placement sections (verified, partially read).
- [FSR 4.1.1 upscaling guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-ml.md) — ML requirements and colourspace rules (verified, partially read).
- [FSR 2.3.0 release notes](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/releases/tag/v2.3.0) — per-effect changes; release API record opened, tag page not opened (link not opened).

## Intel XeSS

### Components and current version

- The current kit is the [XeSS 3 SDK, latest release 3.0.2 published 2026-07-24](https://api.github.com/repos/intel/xess/releases/latest) (verified), with the repository describing itself as the XeSS 3 SDK ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/README.md) (verified)).
- XeSS Super Resolution boosts frame rates on [all GPUs with SM 6.4 DP4a support](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/README.md) (verified).
- XeSS Frame Generation targets [Intel Arc discrete and integrated GPUs plus non-Intel GPUs with SM 6.4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/README.md) (verified); since 2.1 it uses [common Shader Model 6.4 code on non-Intel GPUs](https://www.phoronix.com/news/Intel-XeSS-2-1-Released) (inferred).
- Xe Low Latency is available on [Arc GPUs and on non-Intel GPUs when combined with XeSS-FG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/README.md) (verified); standalone XeLL is [not supported on non-Intel GPUs](https://www.phoronix.com/news/Intel-XeSS-2-1-Released) (inferred).
- XeSS-FG [requires XeLL integration, while SR and XeLL can each be enabled independently](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/README.md) (verified).
- Release 3.0.2 updated XeLL to 1.3.2.10, fixing [minimumIntervalUs units, a non-Intel memory leak and Streamline proxy handling](https://api.github.com/repos/intel/xess/releases/latest) (verified).

### Platforms and requirements

- XeSS-SR supports [DirectX 11, DirectX 12 and Vulkan](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/xess2-whitepaper.html) (inferred), with [API-specific initialisation and execution paths for all three](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_sr_developer_guide_english.md) (verified) and a [Vulkan 1.1 requirement](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/xess-sr-developer-guide.html) (inferred).
- XeSS-FG and XeLL are [designed for DirectX 12](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/xess2-whitepaper.html) (inferred); the FG guide requirements list [Windows 10/11 x64 and DirectX 12 with Intel driver 32.0.101.7029 or later on Arc and Core Ultra families](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_fg_developer_guide_english.md) (verified). Frame generation on Vulkan is [reported as unsupported](https://github.com/peqhub/mcvr/blob/HEAD/docs/XeFG_Research_Report.md) (inferred).
- Operating system support is [Windows 10/11 x64](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_fg_developer_guide_english.md) (verified); the stack is described as [Windows-focused](http://www.phoronix.com/news/Intel-XeSS-SDK-2.0.1) (inferred). Windows on ARM64 is not documented and the x64-only requirements imply it is unsupported (inferred); no Linux or macOS support was found in the sources read (inferred).
- Quality presets run [NativeAA 1.0x, Ultra Quality Plus 1.3x, Ultra Quality 1.5x, Quality 1.7x, Balanced 2.0x, Performance 2.3x and Ultra Performance 3.0x](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_sr_developer_guide_english.md) (verified).

### Inputs

- XeSS-SR takes [jitter with a defined sequence, colour, motion vectors, depth, a responsive pixel mask and mip bias settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_sr_developer_guide_english.md) (verified), with [jitter scale, velocity scale and exposure multiplier controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_sr_developer_guide_english.md) (verified) and [fixed and dynamic input resolution modes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_sr_developer_guide_english.md) (verified). Exact vector, depth and jitter conventions sit in unread portions and are unconfirmed.
- Resource states and formats are [documented per API including Vulkan specifics](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_sr_developer_guide_english.md) (verified); details are unconfirmed here.
- XeSS-FG takes [motion vectors, depth, HUD-less colour and a UI texture with resource tagging and frame constants](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_fg_developer_guide_english.md) (verified), plus [UI composition modes, HDR display support and letterboxing handling](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_fg_developer_guide_english.md) (verified).
- Frame rate targets are [40 FPS minimum and 60 FPS recommended input](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_fg_developer_guide_english.md) (verified); all [VSync and fixed or variable refresh modes are supported](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_fg_developer_guide_english.md) (verified).
- Super resolution runs [before post-processing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_sr_developer_guide_english.md) (verified); frame generation runs [before presentation through a proxy swap chain issuing several presents per rendered frame](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_fg_developer_guide_english.md) (verified).
- XeLL works through [sleep calls and simulation, render-submit and present markers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xell_developer_guide_english.md) (verified), reducing [input-to-render and render-to-screen latency](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xell_developer_guide_english.md) (verified).

### Integration outline

1. Integrate in the recommended order: [SR first, then XeLL, then FG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/README.md) (verified).
2. Initialise SR on the DX11, DX12 or Vulkan path and query [required instance and device extensions and features on Vulkan](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/xess-sr-developer-guide.html) (inferred).
3. Supply the per-frame inputs and scales each dispatch ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_sr_developer_guide_english.md) (verified)).
4. Add XeLL sleep and markers around simulation, submission and present ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xell_developer_guide_english.md) (verified)).
5. Add FG with its [proxy swap chain, external heap options, generated-frame count control and UI handling](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_fg_developer_guide_english.md) (verified); handle [window and swap chain resolution changes and present status](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_fg_developer_guide_english.md) (verified).
6. Verify with the [XeSS Inspector debugging tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/README.md) (verified).

### Licence and redistribution

- SDK binaries are under the [Intel Simplified Software License, October 2022 version](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/LICENSE.txt) (verified), allowing [use and redistribution of the binary-only software without modification, with copyright notice and terms reproduced](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/LICENSE.txt) (verified), [no reverse engineering](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/LICENSE.txt) (verified) and [no Intel endorsement claims](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/LICENSE.txt) (verified).
- Headers are separately under the [MIT licence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/inc/MIT.txt) (verified), in the [xess, xess_fg and xell include directories](https://api.github.com/repos/intel/xess/contents/inc) (verified).
- An open-source project may therefore redistribute the XeSS DLLs unmodified with notices, but the SDK itself remains [closed-source](http://www.phoronix.com/news/Intel-XeSS-SDK-2.0.1) (inferred).

### Pitfalls

- Preset scaling ratios changed in 1.3 and later, so updating integrations must [re-verify scaling, mip bias and jitter sequences](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_sr_developer_guide_english.md) (verified).
- Motion blur should be [disabled or adapted for generated frames](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_fg_developer_guide_english.md) (verified).
- Native D3D12 objects are preferred over proxies for stability ([source](https://api.github.com/repos/intel/xess/releases/latest) (verified)), and code using minimumIntervalUs must account for the [nanoseconds-to-microseconds units fix](https://api.github.com/repos/intel/xess/releases/latest) (verified).
- The guides document [thread safety, error handling, async shader compilation and diagnostic capture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_fg_developer_guide_english.md) (verified) that integrators must follow.

### Official documentation and guides

- [intel/xess repository](https://github.com/intel/xess) — SDK tree, headers, samples and guides; page opened but largely truncated (verified).
- [XeSS 3.0.2 release notes](https://github.com/intel/xess/releases/tag/v3.0.2) — latest changes; release API record opened, tag page not opened (link not opened).
- [XeSS-SR developer guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_sr_developer_guide_english.md) — inputs, formats, init and execution per API (verified, partially read).
- [XeSS-FG developer guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_fg_developer_guide_english.md) — proxy swap chain, UI, HDR and lifecycle (verified, partially read).
- [XeLL developer guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xell_developer_guide_english.md) — sleep, markers and features (verified, partially read).
- [XeSS-SR guide on intel.com](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/xess-sr-developer-guide.html) — same guide as a web page; fetch returned 403 (could not be opened).
- [XeSS 2 whitepaper](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/xess2-whitepaper.html) — API coverage summary; snippet only, not opened (link not opened).
- [XeSS licence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/LICENSE.txt) — binary redistribution terms (verified).
- [Header licence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/inc/MIT.txt) — MIT terms for includes (verified).

## Apple MetalFX

### Components and current version

- MetalFX offers [spatial upscaling from colour alone and temporal upscaling from colour, depth and motion](https://github.com/theapplaunchers/apple-docs-for-rag/blob/HEAD/WWDC2025/api/MetalFX.md) (inferred), via the MTLFXSpatialScaler and MTLFXTemporalScaler effect classes ([source](https://github.com/theapplaunchers/apple-docs-for-rag/blob/HEAD/WWDC2025/api/MetalFX.md) (inferred)).
- Frame interpolation [generates intermediate frames for higher refresh rates](https://dev.to/arshtechpro/wwdc-2025-discover-metal-4-23f2) (inferred) and runs [at the end of the pipeline just before display](https://HotHardware.com/news/apple-unveils-metalfx-frame-interpolation-ai-game-rendering-bandwagon) (inferred).
- The denoised temporal scaler [removes noise from low ray-count renders during upscaling](https://github.com/need2edit/wwdc-journal/blob/HEAD/analysis/essentials-accessibility-media-games.md) (inferred), aimed at [practical ray and path tracing on Apple hardware](https://www.flatpanelshd.com/news.php?subaction=showfull&id=1749809641) (inferred).
- Metal 4 adds MTL4FX-prefixed variants of all four effects, confirmed by the [feature list of the Rust MetalFX bindings](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/objc2-metal-fx) (verified).
- MetalFX is an OS framework without SDK versions; the [MetalFX documentation root](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metalfx) (verified) resolved but returned only a script shell, so class details below come from snippets and mirrors.

### Platforms and requirements

- MetalFX upscaling arrived with [macOS Ventura](https://www.techpowerup.com/295612/apple-announces-macos-ventura-with-new-productivity-gaming-features&lt) (inferred); frame interpolation and denoising arrived with [Metal 4 on macOS Tahoe 26](https://www.tomshardware.com/software/macos/apple-debuts-macos-26-tahoe-at-wwdc-with-liquid-glass-redesign) (inferred). Whether the non-Metal-4 interpolator and denoiser classes work on older systems is disputed in [developer discussion](https://forums.macrumors.com/threads/major-gaming-news-at-wwdc-metal-and-new-games.2347213/page-198) (inferred) and unconfirmed.
- Hardware needs an [M1 minimum on Apple silicon](https://www.tweaktown.com/news/86706/metalfx-upscaling-apples-take-on-nvidia-dlss-amd-fsr-intel-xess/index.html) (inferred); exact per-effect GPU tiers are unconfirmed.
- There is no Windows support; MetalFX is Apple-platform only (inferred). Reaching it from a Vulkan application on MoltenVK requires exporting the underlying Metal objects through [VK_EXT_metal_objects, which exposes vkExportMetalObjectsEXT and Metal-backed VkDeviceMemory, VkImage, VkSemaphore and VkEvent](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Docs/main/appendices/VK_EXT_metal_objects.adoc) (verified) on [Metal-layered implementations only](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Docs/main/appendices/VK_EXT_metal_objects.adoc) (verified).
- Community attempts show the interop is fragile: one project reports [running MetalFX over exported MoltenVK textures could never work because MoltenVK presents after the hook runs](https://github.com/hongyuehao123/metalmod/blob/HEAD/docs/phase7-plan.md) (inferred), while another design [exports the low-resolution texture and queue and presents the MetalFX result in a native overlay](https://github.com/zinedinarnaut/sol/blob/HEAD/Docs/SOL_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md) (inferred). No official Vulkan-to-MetalFX path was found; a native Metal renderer is the documented route (inferred).

### Inputs

- The temporal scaler needs [pixel colour, depth and motion information](https://github.com/theapplaunchers/apple-docs-for-rag/blob/HEAD/WWDC2025/api/MetalFX.md) (inferred); the spatial scaler needs [only colour](https://github.com/theapplaunchers/apple-docs-for-rag/blob/HEAD/WWDC2025/api/MetalFX.md) (inferred).
- Apple's sample shows [adding jitter during rendering and building a motion vector texture](https://developer.apple.com/metal/sample-code/) (inferred); the sample page resolved but its content was not reached (verified).
- Frame interpolation accepts [camera parameters and elapsed time between frames](https://HotHardware.com/news/apple-unveils-metalfx-frame-interpolation-ai-game-rendering-bandwagon) (inferred).
- The denoised scaler path is reported to need [separate colour, depth, motion, albedo, normal and roughness textures](https://github.com/tqjxlm/sparkle/blob/HEAD/docs/Denoiser.md) (inferred).
- Vector, depth and jitter conventions, formats and resolution rules are unconfirmed from primary sources.

### Integration outline

1. Pick [spatial or temporal upscaling based on available inputs](https://github.com/theapplaunchers/apple-docs-for-rag/blob/HEAD/WWDC2025/api/MetalFX.md) (inferred).
2. Render low resolution with jitter and produce depth and motion vector textures ([source](https://developer.apple.com/metal/sample-code/) (inferred)).
3. Configure the matching descriptor and effect, then encode it on the Metal command buffer (inferred from the class model; details unconfirmed).
4. Add frame interpolation late in the frame with camera and timing data ([source](https://HotHardware.com/news/apple-unveils-metalfx-frame-interpolation-ai-game-rendering-bandwagon) (inferred)).
5. For path tracing, route the ray-traced buffers through the denoised scaler ([source](https://github.com/need2edit/wwdc-journal/blob/HEAD/analysis/essentials-accessibility-media-games.md) (inferred)).
6. On MoltenVK, export Metal objects per the extension ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Docs/main/appendices/VK_EXT_metal_objects.adoc) (verified)) and own Metal presentation and cross-queue synchronisation yourself; expect [explicit MTLSharedEvent ordering work](https://github.com/hongyuehao123/metalmod/blob/HEAD/ROADMAP.md) (inferred).

### Licence and redistribution

- MetalFX ships with Apple operating systems under Apple developer terms; there are no redistributable binaries, DLLs or headers to ship (inferred). Exact licence text was not reviewed and is unconfirmed.

### Pitfalls

- The Metal 3 versus Metal 4 class split (MTLFX versus MTL4FX) is confirmed by [binding feature flags](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/objc2-metal-fx) (verified) but version gating per class is unconfirmed; verify availability macros before use.
- Temporal state must be reset on camera and world transitions; at least one engine [invalidates MetalFX history, exposure feedback and motion history together](https://github.com/mbrock/moppe/blob/HEAD/docs/renderer-design.md) (inferred).
- Output textures are reported to require [private storage mode](https://github.com/havokentity/demont-engine/commit/24328c9b6613951e17ad40f3a9c98fe6efa490b0) (inferred).
- Early OS releases had [fixed bugs in MTL4FX denoised and temporal upscaling](https://github.com/averyy/apple-dev-docs/blob/HEAD/documentation/macos-release-notes/macos-26-release-notes.md) (inferred); pin minimum OS versions deliberately.

### Official documentation and guides

- [MetalFX documentation root](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metalfx) — class hub; opened but returned a script shell (verified).
- [Metal sample code](https://developer.apple.com/metal/sample-code/) — includes the temporal AA and upscaling sample; opened but content not reached (verified).
- [WWDC22 Boost performance with MetalFX Upscaling](https://appleinsider.com/articles/23/06/22/understanding-metalfx-apples-graphics-performance-booster) — session title via secondary report; not opened (link not opened).
- [WWDC25 Discover Metal 4](https://dev.to/arshtechpro/wwdc-2025-discover-metal-4-23f2) — frame interpolation and denoising announcement via secondary report; not opened (link not opened).
- [MetalFX API mirror](https://github.com/theapplaunchers/apple-docs-for-rag/blob/HEAD/WWDC2025/api/MetalFX.md) — unofficial Apple docs mirror describing the scaler choice; snippet only, not opened (link not opened).
- [VK_EXT_metal_objects specification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Docs/main/appendices/VK_EXT_metal_objects.adoc) — import and export of Metal objects (verified).

## Ray tracing and path tracing support

- DLSS Ray Reconstruction is the NVIDIA denoiser: an [AI network replacing hand-tuned denoisers between sampled rays](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss) (verified), with transformer architecture in its Streamline plugin ([source](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss) (verified)). It needs an RTX GPU ([source](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss) (verified)); detailed inputs are unconfirmed.
- FSR Ray Regeneration 1.2.0 is the AMD ML denoiser ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/readme.md) (verified)), now covering [ambient occlusion, specular occlusion and checkerboard rendering](https://api.github.com/repos/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/releases/latest) (verified). FSR Radiance Caching is a [technical preview for caching path tracing results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/readme.md) (verified), at [version 0.9.0](https://tech-insider.org/amd-fsr-redstone-setup-2026/) (inferred).
- Intel has no ray-tracing denoiser in the XeSS SDK as far as the sources read show; only [SR, FG and low latency are listed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/README.md) (verified).
- MetalFX denoising is the Apple path for [low ray-count and path-traced content](https://www.flatpanelshd.com/news.php?subaction=showfull&id=1749809641) (inferred), demonstrated with [real-time path tracing](https://www.pcquest.com/news/mac-gaming-2026-apple-gaming-metal-4-game-porting-toolkit-12004351) (inferred).
- MoltenVK does not support Vulkan ray tracing in any release: it is an [almost-complete subset of Vulkan 1.4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/MoltenVK/main/README.md) (verified), and ray tracing exists only as [open, unmerged pull request 2771 implementing the KHR acceleration structure, ray query, ray tracing pipeline, pipeline library and maintenance1 extensions behind an experimental flag](https://api.github.com/repos/KhronosGroup/MoltenVK/pulls/2771) (verified), created 2026-07-12 and still open ([source](https://api.github.com/repos/KhronosGroup/MoltenVK/pulls/2771) (verified)). Third parties confirm the [KHR ray extensions are absent from MoltenVK devices](https://github.com/tagban/moghouse/blob/HEAD/docs/macos-bringup.md) (inferred). Consequence: path tracing on macOS needs native Metal, not MoltenVK Vulkan RT.

## Rust bindings

| Framework | Crate | State | Licence | Link |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DLSS | nvidia-dlss 0.1.0 | [New, RR via NGX on Vulkan](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/nvidia-dlss) (verified) | [MIT or Apache-2.0](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/nvidia-dlss) (verified) | [crates.io](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/nvidia-dlss) (verified) |
| DLSS | nvidia-streamline 0.1.0 | [Sibling crate, details unread](https://github.com/attackgoat/nvidia/blob/HEAD/README.md) (inferred) | Unconfirmed | [repo](https://github.com/attackgoat/nvidia) (inferred) |
| FSR | fidelityfx 0.0.0-dev | [Placeholder package, repo active](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/fidelityfx) (verified) | [MIT](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/fidelityfx) (verified) | [crates.io](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/fidelityfx) (verified) |
| FSR | wgpu-ffx 0.1.0 | [FSR3 upscaler for wgpu](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates?q=fidelityfx&per_page=5) (verified) | Unconfirmed | [repo](https://github.com/cwfitzgerald/wgpu-ffx) (inferred) |
| XeSS | none found | [No crate on crates.io](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/xess) (verified) | Bind MIT headers yourself | [inc dir](https://api.github.com/repos/intel/xess/contents/inc) (verified) |
| MetalFX | objc2-metal-fx 0.3.2 | [Maintained, MTLFX plus MTL4FX](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/objc2-metal-fx) (verified) | [Zlib, Apache-2.0 or MIT](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/objc2-metal-fx) (verified) | [repo](https://github.com/madsmtm/objc2) (verified) |

- nvidia-dlss 0.1.0, published 2026-09-05, is described as [Vulkan bindings for DLSS Ray Reconstruction through NGX](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/nvidia-dlss) (verified), needs [Rust 1.95](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/nvidia-dlss) (verified) and has [18 downloads](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/nvidia-dlss) (verified). Its repository also hosts [Streamline, NRD, OMM and related crates](https://github.com/attackgoat/nvidia/blob/HEAD/README.md) (inferred). No DLSS crate for wgpu was found (inferred).
- The fidelityfx crates are [version 0.0.0-dev placeholders with zero code lines](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/fidelityfx) (verified), but the underlying repository is active with [bindings regenerated against FSR SDK v2.3.0 in July 2026](https://api.github.com/repos/Traverse-Research/fidelityfx-rs/commits?per_page=1) (verified).
- For XeSS with no binding available, the surface to bind is the [xess, xess_fg and xell C headers](https://api.github.com/repos/intel/xess/contents/inc) (verified), which are [MIT licensed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/inc/MIT.txt) (verified), against the [binary-only redistributable libraries](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/LICENSE.txt) (verified).
- For DLSS without the new crates, the surface would be NGX or the Streamline C++ API ([sources](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS) (verified), ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline) (verified)); for FSR, the [five-function FSR API plus backends](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/getting-started/ffx-api.md) (verified).

## How other projects integrated these

- Godot documents [FSR 1.0, FSR2 2.2 and MetalFX spatial viewport scaling modes](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_viewport.html) (inferred; page opened but enum section not reached). Its FSR2 implementation lives in [servers/rendering/renderer_rd/effects/fsr2.cpp with shaders under servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/effects/fsr2 and thirdparty/amd-fsr2](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.4/contributing/development/core_and_modules/internal_rendering_architecture.html) (inferred), with [TAA resolve and motion vector shaders alongside](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.4/contributing/development/core_and_modules/internal_rendering_architecture.html) (inferred). Godot issue 94126 discusses [FSR2 motion vector requirements](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/94126) (inferred).
- Bevy ships [anti-aliasing including TAA](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/commit/cf71f4942db946034874e0b5c6e8ac1009e37bb2) (inferred); no built-in DLSS or FSR integration was found (inferred). A third-party [bevy_dlss5 plugin targets Bevy 0.19.1 on Vulkan](https://github.com/alrikolson/bevy_dlss5) (inferred).
- RT64 is the [N64 renderer project at rt64/rt64](https://api.github.com/repos/rt64/rt64) (verified) with [apple, common, hle, gui and other source trees](https://api.github.com/repos/rt64/rt64/contents/src) (verified); it historically advertised [DLSS, FSR 2 and XeSS support](https://github.com/dariosamo/sm64ex) (inferred), but exact current upscaler files are unconfirmed.
- UnleashedRecomp requires [D3D12 with Shader Model 6 or Vulkan 1.2 on Windows 10 and Linux](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp/main/README.md) (verified) and switches APIs via a [GraphicsAPI config value](https://github.com/hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp/issues/502) (inferred). No DLSS, FSR or XeSS integration in it could be confirmed despite dedicated search.
- LibertyRecomp vendors [NVIDIA DLSS, FidelityFX SDK, FSR 1, SMAA and MoltenVK as submodules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OZORDI/LibertyRecomp/main/.gitmodules) (verified) plus an [XeSS tools directory](https://github.com/ozordi/libertyrecomp/blob/HEAD/tools/xess/doc/xess_sr_developer_guide_english.md) (inferred). Its native temporal rendering work with TAA, FSR, DLSS and MetalFX could not be pinned to specific source files in the time available; start from the [.gitmodules file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OZORDI/LibertyRecomp/main/.gitmodules) (verified) and the [reflection rendering study](https://github.com/ozordi/libertyrecomp/blob/HEAD/docs/reflection-rendering-study/README.md) (inferred).
- OptiScaler is the closest example of several upscalers behind one interface: it [bridges upscaling and frame generation across GPUs with DLSS2+, XeSS and FSR2+ inputs](https://api.github.com/repos/shooterspps/OptiScaler) (verified) across [DirectX 11, 12 and Vulkan](https://github.com/swimreapers/OptiScaler_DLSSNR) (inferred) with [per-API upscaler selection in an INI file](https://github.com/gabrielmaialva33/optiscaler_dlssnr/blob/HEAD/Config.md) (inferred). The original cdozdil/OptiScaler repository [returns 404](https://api.github.com/repos/cdozdil/OptiScaler) (verified); active work continues in forks such as [shooterspps/OptiScaler](https://api.github.com/repos/shooterspps/OptiScaler) (verified).
- Vendor samples covering Vulkan are the [FidelityFX SDK samples](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/readme.md) (verified), the [XeSS samples directory](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/README.md) (verified) and the [DLSS Linux demo archive](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/releases/expanded_assets/v310.9.1) (verified).

## One interface for all four

- A shared abstraction can own the common inputs: render and display resolutions, jitter generation and projection updates, depth and motion vector production, exposure tracking, cut resets, mip bias and the UI split for frame generation, since every framework consumes this class of data ([DLSS](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/blob/main/doc/DLSS_Programming_Guide_Release.pdf) (inferred), [FSR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/Kits/FidelityFX/docs/techniques/super-resolution-upscaler.md) (verified), [XeSS](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_sr_developer_guide_english.md) (verified), [MetalFX](https://github.com/theapplaunchers/apple-docs-for-rag/blob/HEAD/WWDC2025/api/MetalFX.md) (inferred)). Godot's single [scaling mode enum over FSR and MetalFX](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_viewport.html) (inferred) and OptiScaler's [per-API upscaler selection](https://github.com/gabrielmaialva33/optiscaler_dlssnr/blob/HEAD/Config.md) (inferred) show the pattern is viable.
- What cannot be unified: graphics API coverage, since [XeSS frame generation is DirectX 12 only](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_fg_developer_guide_english.md) (verified) and MetalFX is Metal only (inferred); swap chain ownership, since DLSS-G, FSR and XeSS each impose [their own proxy or replacement swap chain](https://github.com/thierbig/bg3fgvk/blob/HEAD/docs/2026-08-27-fgvk-design.md) (inferred) ([FSR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/main/readme.md) (verified), [XeSS](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/doc/xess_fg_developer_guide_english.md) (verified)); hardware gating, since DLSS needs [RTX](https://developer.nvidia.com/rtx/dlss) (verified), FSR 4 ML needs [RDNA3/4](https://github.com/characterecho-sean/edvr-unofficial-patch/blob/HEAD/docs/fsr-upscaler-design-2026-09-16.md) (inferred) and MetalFX needs [Apple silicon](https://www.tweaktown.com/news/86706/metalfx-upscaling-apples-take-on-nvidia-dlss-amd-fsr-intel-xess/index.html) (inferred); and latency companions, since [Reflex must not be active under foreign frame generation](https://github.com/NVIDIA-RTX/Streamline/raw/refs/heads/main/docs/RTX%20UI%20Developer%20Guidelines.pdf?download=) (inferred) while [XeSS-FG mandates XeLL](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/intel/xess/main/README.md) (verified).
- Practical consequence for the stated targets: on Windows x64 all of DLSS, FSR and XeSS-SR are candidates with FG available from DLSS and FSR; on Windows ARM64 only the portable FSR path looks plausible and needs a source rebuild ([sources](https://www.pcgamer.com/hardware/gaming-laptops/qualcomms-new-windows-pc-chip-supports-amds-fsr-and-im-not-sure-amd-had-any-idea-about-it/) (inferred), ([source](https://github.com/justradical/sloptiscaler/blob/HEAD/arm64ec/README.md) (inferred)); on macOS only MetalFX applies, most robustly behind a native Metal renderer given the [fragile MoltenVK interop reports](https://github.com/hongyuehao123/metalmod/blob/HEAD/docs/phase7-plan.md) (inferred).

## Open questions

- DLSS motion vector sign, units and resolution conventions; depth convention and precision; reactive or transparency mask support; Ray Reconstruction input set; per-mode resolution limits; dynamic-resolution rules; Linux driver and Vulkan version floor beyond the sample archive.
- Whether the neural rendering runtime behind DLSS 5 (nvngx_dlssnr.dll) is available in any public SDK, and its integration contract.
- Whether any nvngx binary runs on Windows ARM64, and which plugins the Streamline aarch64 and arm64ec archives actually contain.
- FSR motion vector, depth, jitter and exposure conventions in detail; Vulkan support for the ML upscaler, ML frame generation, ray regeneration and radiance caching; the current SDK-wide licence and ML DLL redistribution terms; FSR behaviour on macOS.
- XeSS-SR motion vector, depth and jitter conventions in detail; resource format tables; any Linux, ARM64 or macOS story.
- Per-class MetalFX availability macros and GPU tiers; exact input texture conventions; any official Vulkan-on-MoltenVK guidance.
- Godot MetalFX temporal support beyond spatial mode, if any; UnleashedRecomp upscaler status; LibertyRecomp temporal file paths; RT64 current upscaler file paths; wgpu-ffx licence; Bevy built-in upscaler plans.
```

`plan.md`:

```md
# LibertyFlux plan

Status: phase 0 can start; the game is installed. Last updated 2026-10-03.

## Goal

Grand Theft Auto IV's engine rewritten in Rust, function by function, so the game runs as a native
64-bit program at hundreds of frames per second, with room for new gameplay and graphics.

The Rust port exists to make the game 64-bit and portable (Cam, 2026-10-03).

| Target | Graphics | Upscaling and frame generation |
|---|---|---|
| Windows x64 | Vulkan, D3D12 optional | DLSS and FSR for upscaling and frame generation; XeSS for upscaling |
| Windows ARM64 | Vulkan | FSR only, and it needs a source rebuild (inferred). DLSS is reported unsupported; XeSS documents x64 only |
| macOS (Apple silicon) | MoltenVK first, native Metal for MetalFX and ray tracing | MetalFX. FSR on macOS is unconfirmed |

Also wanted: no redistributable installs (.NET, Visual C++ runtime, DirectX end-user runtime), and
path tracing as a stretch goal.

The upscaler research is in `documentation/upscaling-and-frame-generation.md`, with a source link
and a verified or inferred label on every claim. What it changes here:

- DLSS 5 exists (NVIDIA developer blog, 22 September 2026): neural rendering that needs an RTX 50
  series GPU. The blog does not say an SDK is available to developers yet, so plan on DLSS 4.5
  through the Streamline SDK and treat DLSS 5 as unavailable until an SDK ships.
- XeSS frame generation is DirectX 12 only. With a Vulkan renderer we get XeSS upscaling but not
  its frame generation, unless the optional D3D12 backend is built.
- Every frame generation framework takes over presentation with its own swap chain, so the
  renderer must not assume it owns the swap chain.
- MoltenVK has no ray tracing in any release (an open pull request only), so path tracing on macOS
  needs the native Metal backend. MetalFX is Metal only and reaching it through MoltenVK is fragile.
- Rust bindings exist for MetalFX (maintained) and are new or placeholder for DLSS and FSR; XeSS
  has none. Expect to write or generate bindings against the C headers.
- Not yet established: the exact motion vector, depth and jitter conventions for each framework.
  The research lane could not read the long guides in full. A follow-up lane with a working shell
  should read them from cloned repositories before the renderer is designed.

## Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| What is committed | Structures, symbols, Rust rewrites, tooling, docs. Never decompiled code | Cam's rule, in AGENTS.md |
| Intermediate C++ stage | None. Lanes read decompiler output from `.artifacts/` and write Rust directly | Decompiled C++ cannot be committed, and an uncommitted months-long intermediate is a loss risk. Removes a phase |
| How a function is checked | Native side-by-side run: a small 32-bit helper process maps the original executable's code, calls the original function and the 32-bit Rust build of the rewrite with the same inputs and starting memory, and compares results, memory writes and outgoing calls | Byte-matching is impossible for Rust. The planned CPU emulator (Unicorn) crashes on every run on this machine, and two lanes confirmed it independently. Native runs were proven on 2026-10-03: two Rust rewrites agreed with their originals on 200 of 200 trials each. Faster than emulation, and it does not need the game itself to run |
| Second check | Accepted functions are swapped into the running game through an injected 32-bit DLL with a per-function switch | Catches what unit comparison misses; a regression is found by switching replacements off in halves |
| Target binary | The Steam Complete Edition executable (1.2.0.x) | Cam owns it and it runs without a cracked launcher. FusionFix and scrDbg already support it |
| Older builds | 1.0.8.0 is used only for static analysis, if an official patch executable is available, to carry names across with Ghidra Version Tracking | IV-SDK and most public class knowledge target 1.0.7.0 and 1.0.8.0. Downgrading the installed game needs a cracked launcher, which we are not doing |
| Xbox 360 recompilation | Not our base. Used as a reference for class names, virtual table order and engine documentation | Its output keeps the PowerPC machine model permanently and cannot become clean Rust |
| Third-party libraries | Identified by signature and excluded from the queue until phase 5, then replaced | See "Dependencies" |
| Parallelism | Lanes write only to their own scratch folder; the coordinator integrates | No git worktrees, no stash |
| Where the investigation data lives | One SQLite database under `.artifacts/db/` for functions, names, evidence, claims, attempts and verdicts, with a deterministic JSON export committed to the repository | Dozens of lanes read and write at once and claims must be atomic, which loose files do badly. Git cannot diff a database, and the database holds addresses, so the tracked form is a sorted text export |
| Publishing | Cam's decision. README and a GitHub Pages site exist locally; nothing is pushed until Cam asks | The Modern Warfare 2 project lost its hosting and its agents' work after takedowns in September 2026 |

## Model routing

Set by Cam on 2026-10-03.

| Model | How it runs | Work |
|---|---|---|
| Opus 5.5 | This session | Coordination only: plan, harness and checker design, review of anything that changes the checker or shared structures, audit samples, wave sign-off |
| Muse Spark 1.3, max effort | `muse exec --model muse-spark-1.3-contributor --reasoning-effort max`, one background task per lane | Everything else by default |
| Sonnet | Agent tool | Second pass on functions Muse deferred, task classes where Muse's numbers fall short, and design critique |

"Struggling" is measured per task class: accept rate, attempts per accept, false accepts found by audit.

Muse track record so far: seven research lanes. Spot-checks of lane A against two cited source
files matched exactly. Lane H (dependencies) was mostly inferred from forum posts and said so.
Muse lanes could not run shell commands in their sandbox; that must be fixed before phase 1
(`muse sandbox`, workspace trust).

## This machine

- ARM64: Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme, Adreno X2-90, fanless. The original game is 32-bit x86 and
  runs under emulation here.
- Visual Studio Build Tools 2026, MSVC 14.51 with x86, x64 and ARM64 targets. Windows SDK 10.0.26100
  with x86 libraries. CMake, Ninja, Python 3.11 (x64).
- GTA IV is installed through Steam as of 2026-10-03: Complete Edition, version 1.2.0.59. Its
  location and other machine-specific details are in the untracked `notes.md`.

Installed for this project on 2026-10-03:

| Tool | Where | Checked by |
|---|---|---|
| Rust target `i686-pc-windows-msvc` | rustup | Built a 32-bit DLL exporting a `thiscall` function |
| Temurin JDK 21.0.12 x64 | `tools\jdk` | SHA-256 matched Adoptium; `java -version` runs |
| Ghidra 12.1.4 | `tools\ghidra` | SHA-256 listed in the official release notes; headless import and full analysis of a 32-bit program succeeded |
| `pefile`, `capstone`, `pyghidra` | `.venv` | pip install succeeded |

Ghidra needs `JAVA_HOME` set to `tools\jdk`. The JDK is x64 on purpose: Ghidra ships Windows native
components for x64 only.

Unicorn was installed and then abandoned: it crashes on start under this machine's x64 emulation.
The checker runs code natively in a 32-bit helper process instead.

## Phases

| Phase | Work | Exit gate |
|---|---|---|
| 0. Measure | See task list below | Function count, library and game split, compiler version, class list, and a yes or no on whether the game runs here |
| 1. Harness | Work queue, context packets, emulator comparison, injected DLL with per-function switch, lane permissions, progress log | 50 functions accepted end to end by one lane |
| 2. Pilot | 3 Muse lanes plus a reviewer for a few days; Sonnet on the deferred set | Measured functions per day and false-accept rate; routing confirmed or changed |
| 3. Rewrite | 10 to 20 lanes; full regression and a checkpoint commit between waves | Every game function has an accepted Rust rewrite; the game plays with every switch on |
| 4. Standalone | Build the Rust code as its own 32-bit program. This is a test configuration | It runs without the original executable |
| 5. 64-bit | Converting resource loader, script VM pointer handles, platform layer replacing Win32, replacements for every third-party library | Windows x64 and Windows ARM64 builds play |
| 6. Renderer | Vulkan renderer with motion vectors, depth and jitter outputs; fixed-timestep simulation; macOS | Frame-rate target measured on all three platforms |
| 7. Upscalers and new work | DLSS, FSR, XeSS, MetalFX behind one interface; frame generation; new gameplay and graphics; path tracing | Each upscaler verified on hardware that supports it |

Status on 2026-10-04: phase 3 is under way. The gates before it were met as follows.

- Phase 0: every item is measured except whether the game runs on this machine. That check needs the
  owner to start the game and is carried as an open item; it also gates reading the encrypted megabyte.
- Phase 1: the queue, the checker (now version 2), the loader and the capture tool exist and are proven
  outside the game. One re-run lane took 201 functions end to end. The per-function switch inside the
  running game is built and tested without the game, and is untested with it.
- Phase 2: two timed pilots of 130 functions, then a production wave. Measured so far: about two minutes
  per verified function under 250 bytes and about eighteen minutes for larger ones; the first 800
  rewrites re-run under checker version 2 all passed, so no false accept has been found. Muse lanes at
  maximum effort carry the work; nothing has needed Sonnet yet.

Phase 3 differs from the plan as first written: about 45 lanes run at once (the machine's measured
ceiling), rewrites are committed to `rewrites/pending/` on every coordinator tick instead of between
waves, and the regression between waves is the re-run of every rewrite under the current checker.

Phases 0 to 4 are faithful reconstruction. No 64-bit or renderer work before the phase 4 gate; the
Modern Warfare 2 project found that mixing those goals stalled the lanes.

Rust written in phase 3 must be pointer-width independent from the first line, even though it is
checked in a 32-bit build. The 32-bit build is the only configuration where the original and the
rewrite share memory layouts and can be compared.

Path tracing needs ray-tracing acceleration structures over the world geometry, materials converted
from the game's Direct3D 9 shaders into a form a path tracer can shade, and a denoiser (DLSS Ray
Reconstruction, FSR Ray Regeneration, or MetalFX's denoising scaler; XeSS has none). MoltenVK has
no ray tracing in any release, so path tracing on macOS needs the native Metal backend.

## Phase 0 findings so far

First look at the executable on 2026-10-03, from its headers only (a copy sits in `orig/`). Verified
by reading the file with `pefile`, except where marked.

| Fact | Value | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| Version and size | 1.2.0.59, 17,425,752 bytes | The current Steam Complete Edition build |
| SHA-256 | `08759a5516f9837920ea504436236bbab89d0826a8e4d04ff106345177b5345d` | Identifies the exact build all addresses refer to |
| Built | Link timestamp 1674831669 (27 January 2023), linker version 11.0 | Rebuilt with Visual Studio 2012, not the 2005-era compiler the original 2008 release used. Ghidra's stock library signatures cover that version |
| Link-time code generation | The compiler record lists 796 objects under the product ID normally used for C++ compiled with link-time code generation, and 653 without (inferred from the standard product ID table) | The risk in the plan is real: a large part of the code was optimised across function boundaries |
| Code size | `.text` is 10.95 MB. Measured in windows, the first 1,028,096 bytes have entropy 8.00 and the rest 5.6 to 6.6 | Corrected: the first megabyte, about 9% of the code, is encrypted on disk. The other 9.9 MB is ordinary code that static analysis can read. The section named `.tbm` is a byte-identical copy of the encrypted range |
| Encrypted range | Opaque to every tool until it has been read from the running game; excluded from counts and from the queue until then | Decided by Cam on 2026-10-03: it will be read from his own running, purchased copy and analysed like the rest. The result is game code and stays in the ignored folders. This needs Cam to start the game once |
| Entry point | In a 657-byte writable, executable section named `.rkstr`, next to a 1 MB section `.tbm` with entropy 8.00 | A Rockstar start-up stub runs before the game, with an encrypted or compressed blob beside it. What it does is unknown; it matters for running the game with replacements injected |
| Type information | 3,618 type descriptor strings | Class names are present, as hoped. The Xbox 360 build has 3,332 |
| Relocations | Present, 1.27 MB | Every absolute address reference is listed, which helps reference resolution |
| Debug record | Names a PDB file, `GTA4_Win32_Final.pdb` | Confirms no symbols ship; only the file name survives |
| C runtime | No runtime DLL imported | Statically linked. No Visual C++ redistributable is needed by the engine |

Imports settle most of the dependency questions:

| Imported | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `d3d9.dll` (1 function), no `d3dx9` | Direct3D 9 only. The helper library is statically linked or unused, so no DirectX end-user runtime |
| `DSOUND.dll` (4) | Audio output is DirectSound, not XAudio2 or OpenAL |
| `DINPUT8.dll` (1), no XInput | Input goes through DirectInput. Gamepad support through XInput, if any, is loaded at run time |
| `binkw32.dll` (16) | Bink video, version 1.9r |
| `WMVCore.DLL` (2) | Windows Media, for user music or replay export |
| `WS2_32.dll` (27) | The engine uses sockets directly |
| `WINTRUST.dll`, `CRYPT32.dll` | Signature and certificate checks, probably for the start-up stub |
| No `xlive.dll`, no .NET, no Social Club import | Confirms those are gone from this build or loaded only by the launcher |

Shipped beside the executable: a launcher (`PlayGTAIV.exe`), `gtaEncoder.exe`, `steam_api.dll` and
`MTLX.dll`. The last two are not in the import table, so they are loaded at run time.

Still to do in phase 0: everything from task 3 onward.

## Phase 0 tasks

1. Install GTA IV from Steam. (Cam)
2. Record the executable: version, size, hash. Check for a DRM or launcher wrapper around it.
3. Run the game on this machine with its own Direct3D 9. Note whether it reaches gameplay and at
   what frame rate. DXVK on Snapdragon under Windows has an open failure report, so do not assume it.
4. Read the compiler and linker version from the executable's Rich header. Look for link-time
   code generation markers.
5. Dump the import tables, delay-load imports and runtime-loaded libraries of the executable and
   every DLL and launcher in the game folder. Classify each as engine, launcher only, DRM or online
   service.
6. Run Ghidra headless analysis. Export the function inventory, cross-references and call graph
   to JSON under `.artifacts/cache`.
7. Tag library code with Ghidra Function ID. This build was linked with Visual Studio 2012, which
   Ghidra's stock databases cover, so try those first. Older library code is also linked in (the
   compiler record shows objects from Visual C++ 2003, 2005, 2008 and 2010 toolchains); if the stock
   databases miss it, build one from the matching static libraries. Ghidra cannot import `.lib`
   files directly; extract the object files first.
8. Recover class names and virtual tables from runtime type information with Ghidra's built-in
   class recovery scripts. Export the hierarchy.
9. Collect names:
   - the script engine layout and ten byte patterns from scrDbg, which targets this build;
   - the three public databases of script-callable functions, cross-checked against each other,
     since some entries are debug functions stripped from release builds;
   - strings, assertion text and `Class::Method` debug strings;
   - IV-SDK and IV:MP class headers, as names and layouts only;
   - Xbox 360 class names carried across by matching virtual table slot order.
10. Find functions reachable only through pointer tables, virtual tables and static constructors.
11. Write the findings into this file and into `docs/data/progress.json`, and revise the estimate.

Tasks 5 to 10 go to Muse lanes once their sandbox can run commands. Tasks 2 to 4 and 11 stay with
the coordinator.

## Harness design

Taken from the projects reviewed. Numbers are Thief 3's unless stated.

- Queue: a script orders functions easiest first by instruction count, branches, calls, switches
  and exception frames. Lanes do not choose.
- Claims: one file per claimed function, created atomically, expiring after 2 hours unless renewed
  by an attempt.
- Context packet per function: the target's disassembly and decompiler output, resolved references
  with names, the structures it touches, the most similar accepted functions with their Rust
  source, names that accepted callers already use for it, and the best earlier attempt on a second
  pass.
- Similarity: Ghidra BSim. The tool the Snowboard Kids project used has no x86 support.
- Families: functions with identical bytes after masking references are grouped. One accepted
  member is stamped onto the rest and passed through the same gate with no model call.
- Attempt budget: cap of 12 per claim, stop after 4 attempts with no improvement. Thief 3's logs
  show 77% of the functions tried matched on the first attempt, then 65%, 37%, 39% and 23% of
  those reaching a second to fifth attempt.
- Deferring is a normal outcome, recorded with a blocker tag. Deferred functions go to Sonnet.
- Lane permissions enforced by tooling: lanes write only under `.artifacts/scratch`, may run only
  the queue, context, try and accept commands, and cannot touch the checker, the symbol tables,
  shared structures or git.
- Lint on every candidate: no inline assembly, no hard-coded original addresses, no stubs.
- Structure definitions carry compile-time size and offset assertions, as gta-reversed does.
- Every batch ends with a sweep that releases stale claims and appends cost, attempts and deferral
  reasons to a ledger.
- Evidence labels on every written finding: Verified, Inferred or Unknown.
- All iteration is local. decomp.me blocks scripted clients and forbids agent-driven requests.

Known weakness of the emulator comparison: floating-point results can differ in the last bits
between the original's code and Rust's, so those comparisons need a tolerance, and a tolerance can
hide a real difference. The in-game switch is the backstop.

## What the research changed

- Size: three pipelines count 31,782, 35,888 and 36,409 functions in the Xbox 360 build. Expect
  the PC build to be the same order, about twice Modern Warfare 2's 16,324.
- No symbols exist anywhere for the PC executable. The Xbox 360 build has real class names in its
  type information but no real function names.
- Names and addresses from older builds do not transfer by byte pattern: one audit found nine of
  nine older patches matched nothing on the current Steam build.
- Game logic is tied to frame time in many places: vehicle handling, Euphoria, pathfinding,
  helicopters, cameras, water, and at least one script function. FusionFix's fix list is the
  starting list of regression tests for the fixed-timestep work.
- Resource files are memory images whose pointers are 28-bit offsets plus a 4-bit block type. An
  unlicensed Rust crate already reads and writes the archive formats.
- Nothing public documents the render thread split or how Euphoria is integrated. Both need
  first-hand analysis.
- Licences: IV-SDK, IV:MP and LibertyRecomp are GPL; FiveM's resource loader is reference-only.
  Read for names and layouts; copy no code.

## Pitfalls from the recompilation projects' history

From lane F, which read all 240 commits of LibertyRecomp's GTA IV history and the second project's
notes. Their bugs are mostly specific to translating PowerPC code; the patterns are not.

| What happened to them | What we do about it |
|---|---|
| Seven subsystem stubs and a loading-gate bypass, added to reach boot, were never verifiably replaced | A stub is never an accepted function. Anything stubbed to make the standalone build boot is a queue row with a blocker tag, counted as not rewritten |
| Rendering was the long pole: first-draw work ran January to April and ended in a revert; the game only became visible after the renderer was rewritten | Treat phase 6 as the largest single phase. Start its design notes during phase 3, without writing renderer code before the phase 4 gate |
| A crash was investigated for weeks as a use-after-free by 14 agents; the "poison" bytes were a legitimate colour and the real bug was an unhooked function | No fix without proof: a before and after log comparison or a caller trace that shows the cause. Agent conclusions need a runnable check |
| Their own hooks broke what they instrumented: a zeroed frame counter, a skipped increment, hooks on the wrong function. Audits later removed about 150 dead or harmful hooks | Every replacement swapped into the running game must preserve the original's side effects, which is what the emulator comparison checks. Diagnostic hooks stay out of tracked code |
| Wrong function addresses and boundaries failed silently and cascaded (two wrong library addresses corrupted about 300 call sites) | Function boundaries and library tags are verified in phase 0 and treated as shared truth that lanes cannot edit |
| The player fell through roads that rendered correctly, in both projects; one is still stuck after two months | Rendering proves nothing about collision. Phase 4's gate includes standing and driving on streamed-in world geometry |
| Async file reads were served synchronously, hiding completion-path bugs the streaming system depends on | The platform layer in phase 5 implements real asynchronous reads |
| About 400 stray debug prints caused a major slowdown; gigabyte logs | Diagnostics live under `.artifacts/` and are stripped before commit |
| 54 research documents in one cycle with no behavioural change shipped | Research ends in a decision or a check recorded in the devlog, not a pile of documents |
| History was rewritten and branches deleted, which stranded forks and destroyed forensics; a 1,056-file accidental deletion needed a restore commit | Never rewrite history. Small, described commits, each with a changelog entry |
| Research documents were deleted in cleanup commits | The devlog is the durable home for findings |

Engine behaviour they documented on the Xbox 360 build, to confirm on PC rather than assume: a boot
sequence that initialises 63 subsystems before a loading gate and the main loop; worker threads
split between rendering, streaming and resource loading; a streaming system with a registry of
24-byte records, 8 load slots and per-type fix-up callbacks; a present gate that stalls if frames
are submitted faster than they are presented; and timing constants where one wrong value freezes
every time-gated task. They did not document which script threads must run for the world to appear.

## Risks

- The emulator comparison is our own design, not a method another project has proven at this scale.
  Phase 1's 50-function gate is where it is tested.
- The game may not run under emulation on this machine, which would remove the in-game check here.
- Functions over about 1,000 instructions and vector-math functions stalled every project reviewed.
- If the executable was built with link-time code generation, function boundaries and calling
  conventions are less regular, which makes both analysis and comparison harder.
- Estimate: Modern Warfare 2 took about ten weeks to playable for 16,324 functions with 4 to 17
  lanes. This is about twice the size, in a different language, with no symbols. Phase 2 measures it.

## Open questions

- Is an x86 Windows PC available if the game does not run here?
- Does Cam want the repository published, and if so where and when?
- Which script threads must run for the world to appear? Neither recompilation project documented it.
```

`rewrites/pending/functions/fn_005195d0.rs`:

```rs
// original: 0x005195d0 rage::rlConcreteLeaderboardInfo<player_schema::Leaderboard_Ranked_Race10NoHolds, player_schema::LeaderboardInfo, 10>::vf7
/// Row lookup for one ranked leaderboard (`vf7 Race10`).
///
/// Fetches the leaderboard tables, fails with -1 when the fetch step reports
/// failure (low byte of its answer), else returns the row pointer at `index`.
/// The original tests only the low byte of the fetch answer.
/// Leaderboard id: 0x67.
export!(stdcall, rw_005195d0(index: u32) -> u32 {
    unsafe {
        const LEADERBOARD_ID: u32 = 0x67;
        let mut frame = [0u32; 6];
        let fetch: extern "fastcall" fn(u32, u32) -> u32 =
            core::mem::transmute(callee_addr(1) as usize);
        if (fetch(LEADERBOARD_ID, frame.as_mut_ptr() as u32) & 0xFF) == 0 {
            return 0xFFFF_FFFF;
        }
        let rows = frame.as_ptr().add(4).read();
        (rows.wrapping_add(index.wrapping_mul(4)) as *const u32).read()
    }
});
```

`rewrites/pending/functions/fn_00519610.rs`:

```rs
// original: 0x00519610 rage::rlConcreteLeaderboardInfo<player_schema::Leaderboard_Ranked_Race10NoHolds, player_schema::LeaderboardInfo, 10>::vf8
/// Column-width query for one ranked leaderboard (`vf8 Race10`).
///
/// Fetches the tables, loads the key at `index`, classifies it through the
/// shared classify step, and maps the class to a width: class 1 takes 4,
/// classes 2-3 take 8, class 5 takes 4, anything else (including failure or
/// an unknown class) takes 0.
/// Leaderboard id: 0x67.
export!(stdcall, rw_00519610(index: u32) -> u32 {
    unsafe {
        const LEADERBOARD_ID: u32 = 0x67;
        let mut frame = [0u32; 6];
        let fetch: extern "fastcall" fn(u32, u32) -> u32 =
            core::mem::transmute(callee_addr(1) as usize);
        if (fetch(LEADERBOARD_ID, frame.as_mut_ptr() as u32) & 0xFF) == 0 {
            return 0;
        }
        let keys = frame.as_ptr().add(5).read();
        let key = (keys.wrapping_add(index.wrapping_mul(4)) as *const u32).read();
        let classify: extern "thiscall" fn(u32) -> u32 =
            core::mem::transmute(callee_addr(2) as usize);
        let class = classify(key);
        if class == 0xFFFF_FFFF {
            return 0;
        }
        match class.wrapping_sub(1) {
            0 => 4,
            1 | 2 => 8,
            3 => 0,
            4 => 4,
            _ => 0,
        }
    }
});

```

`rewrites/pending/functions/fn_00519770.rs`:

```rs
// original: 0x00519770 rage::rlConcreteLeaderboardInfo<player_schema::Leaderboard_Ranked_Race11NoHolds, player_schema::LeaderboardInfo, 10>::vf12
/// Reverse row search for one ranked leaderboard (`vf12 Race11`).
///
/// Fetches the tables, loads the row id at `index`, and scans the id array
/// for it, returning the position. Returns -1 when the fetch fails, when the
/// loaded id is -1, when the array is empty, or when the id is absent.
/// Leaderboard id: 0x68.
export!(stdcall, rw_00519770(index: u32) -> u32 {
    unsafe {
        const LEADERBOARD_ID: u32 = 0x68;
        let mut frame = [0u32; 6];
        let fetch: extern "fastcall" fn(u32, u32) -> u32 =
            core::mem::transmute(callee_addr(1) as usize);
        if (fetch(LEADERBOARD_ID, frame.as_mut_ptr() as u32) & 0xFF) == 0 {
            return 0xFFFF_FFFF;
        }
        let rows = frame.as_ptr().add(5).read();
        let want = (rows.wrapping_add(index.wrapping_mul(4)) as *const u32).read();
        if want == 0xFFFF_FFFF {
            return 0xFFFF_FFFF;
        }
        let count = frame.as_ptr().add(1).read();
        if count == 0 {
            return 0xFFFF_FFFF;
        }
        let ids = frame.as_ptr().add(2).read() as *const u32;
        let mut i = 0u32;
        while i < count {
            if ids.add(i as usize).read() == want {
                return i;
            }
            i = i.wrapping_add(1);
        }
        0xFFFF_FFFF
    }
});

```

`rewrites/pending/functions/fn_005197e0.rs`:

```rs
// original: 0x005197e0 rage::rlConcreteLeaderboardInfo<player_schema::Leaderboard_Ranked_Race11NoHolds, player_schema::LeaderboardInfo, 10>::vf13
/// Value lookup by id for one ranked leaderboard (`vf13 Race11`).
///
/// Fetches the tables and scans the id array for `id`, returning the value
/// from the parallel value array at the match. Returns -1 when the fetch
/// fails, when the count is not positive (signed), or when the id is absent.
/// The original re-checks the found index against -1 after the loop, which is
/// unreachable (the index counts up from 0) and is not repeated here.
/// Leaderboard id: 0x68.
export!(stdcall, rw_005197e0(id: u32) -> u32 {
    unsafe {
        const LEADERBOARD_ID: u32 = 0x68;
        let mut frame = [0u32; 6];
        let fetch: extern "fastcall" fn(u32, u32) -> u32 =
            core::mem::transmute(callee_addr(1) as usize);
        if (fetch(LEADERBOARD_ID, frame.as_mut_ptr() as u32) & 0xFF) == 0 {
            return 0xFFFF_FFFF;
        }
        let count = frame.as_ptr().add(3).read() as i32;
        if count <= 0 {
            return 0xFFFF_FFFF;
        }
        let ids = frame.as_ptr().add(4).read() as *const u32;
        let mut i = 0i32;
        loop {
            if i >= count {
                return 0xFFFF_FFFF;
            }
            if ids.add(i as usize).read() == id {
                break;
            }
            i = i.wrapping_add(1);
        }
        let values = frame.as_ptr().add(5).read();
        (values.wrapping_add((i as u32).wrapping_mul(4)) as *const u32).read()
    }
});

```

```rs
// original: 0x005e4320 NativeImpl_CREATE_HTML_SCRIPT_OBJECT
// rw_005e4320: create an HTML script object and seed its default text.
//
// Allocates a pool slot through the pool allocator, initializes the text
// header (empty length, cleared flags), derives the slot index from the
// object address with signed division, and appends the default string.
// Returns the new slot index.
export!(stdcall, rw_005e4320(arg: u32) -> u32 {
    unsafe {
        let pool = relocated(POOL_BASE);
        let obj: u32 = callee_thiscall!(1, u32, pool);
        callee_cdecl!(2, u32, obj, arg, 0x20);
        *(obj.wrapping_add(OBJ_LEN) as *mut u32) = 0;
        *(obj.wrapping_add(OBJ_TEXT) as *mut u8) = 0;
        *(obj.wrapping_add(OBJ_FLAG) as *mut u8) = 0;
        let base = *global::<u32>(POOL_BASE);
        let stride = *global::<u32>(POOL_STRIDE);
        // Matches `cdq; idiv m32`: 64-bit signed dividend from the address
        // difference, 32-bit signed divisor. Contracts keep the divisor
        // nonzero with a fitting quotient, exactly like the game's pool.
        let diff = obj.wrapping_sub(base) as i32 as i64;
        let index = (diff / (stride as i32 as i64)) as u32;
        callee_stdcall!(3, u32, index, relocated(DEFAULT_TEXT));
        index
    }
});
```

`rewrites/pending/functions/fn_005e43f0.rs`:

```rs
// original: 0x005e43f0 pool_find_matching_slot
// rw_005e43f0: find the topmost live pool slot whose probe accepts.
//
// Scans the script-object pool from slot `count - 1` down, skipping dead
// slots, and probes each live slot's entry with the match callback. The
// callback answers zero on a match; the first match wins and its index is
// returned, otherwise zero (which also covers the empty pool).
export!(stdcall, rw_005e43f0(arg: u32) -> u32 {
    unsafe {
        let mut n = *global::<u32>(POOL_COUNT);
        if n == 0 {
            return 0;
        }
        let bitmap = *global::<u32>(POOL_BITMAP) as *const u8;
        let stride = *global::<u32>(POOL_STRIDE);
        let base = *global::<u32>(POOL_BASE);
        loop {
            n = n.wrapping_sub(1);
            if *bitmap.add(n as usize) & SLOT_DEAD == 0 {
                let entry = base.wrapping_add(stride.wrapping_mul(n));
                if entry != 0 {
                    let probe: u32 = callee_cdecl!(1, u32, entry, arg, 0x20);
                    if probe == 0 {
                        return n;
                    }
                }
            }
            if n == 0 {
                return 0;
            }
        }
    }
});

```

```rs
// original: 0x005e4440 Impl_CONVERT_THEN_ADD_STRING_TO_HTML_SCRIPT_OBJECT
// rw_005e4440: append a string to an HTML script object's text buffer.
//
// Resolves pool slot `index` (dead slots address slot 0, matching the
// original's flag test), measures the source string, copies it with its
// terminator at the end of the live text, and advances the live length.
// Returns the source pointer just past the copied terminator.
export!(stdcall, rw_005e4440(index: u32, src: *const u8) -> u32 {
    unsafe {
        let bitmap = *global::<u32>(POOL_BITMAP) as *const u8;
        let entry: u32 = if *bitmap.add(index as usize) & SLOT_DEAD != 0 {
            0
        } else {
            let stride = *global::<u32>(POOL_STRIDE);
            let base = *global::<u32>(POOL_BASE);
            base.wrapping_add(stride.wrapping_mul(index))
        };
        let mut len = 0u32;
        while *src.add(len as usize) != 0 {
            len = len.wrapping_add(1);
        }
        let used = *(entry.wrapping_add(OBJ_LEN) as *const u32);
        let dst = (entry.wrapping_add(OBJ_TEXT).wrapping_add(used)) as *mut u8;
        let mut i = 0usize;
        loop {
            let b = *src.add(i);
            *dst.add(i) = b;
            i += 1;
            if b == 0 {
                break;
            }
        }
        *(entry.wrapping_add(OBJ_LEN) as *mut u32) = used.wrapping_add(len);
        (src as u32).wrapping_add(len).wrapping_add(1)
    }
```

`rewrites/pending/functions/fn_005e5f80.rs`:

```rs
// original: 0x005e5f80 hash_table_find_string
// rw_005e5f80: look up a string key in a chained hash table.
//
// Hashes the key, picks the bucket by remainder, and walks the chain
// comparing full strings; an empty tag selects the shared empty string on
// either side. Returns the value pointer of the first match, or null.
export!(thiscall, rw_005e5f80(this: u32, key: u32) -> u32 {
    unsafe {
        const EMPTY: u32 = 0xFC9C85;
        let obj = this as *const u8;
        let count = *((obj.add(4)) as *const u16);
        if count == 0 {
            return 0;
        }
        let key_tag = *((key as *const u8).add(4) as *const u16);
        let key_text = if key_tag == 0 {
            relocated(EMPTY)
        } else {
            *(key as *const u32)
        };
        let hash: u32 = callee_cdecl!(1, u32, key_text);
        let table = *(this as *const u32) as *const u32;
        let mut node = *table.add((hash % count as u32) as usize);
        while node != 0 {
            let tag = *((node as *const u8).add(4) as *const u16);
            let text = if tag == 0 {
                relocated(EMPTY)
            } else {
                *(node as *const u32)
            };
            let canon: u32 = callee_thiscall!(2, u32, key);
            let mut i = 0usize;
            let same = loop {
                let x = *((canon as *const u8).add(i));
                let y = *((text as *const u8).add(i));
                if x != y {
                    break false;
                }
                if x == 0 {
                    break true;
                }
                i += 1;
            };
            if same {
                return node.wrapping_add(8);
            }
            node = *((node as *const u8).add(0xC) as *const u32);
        }
        0
    }
});
```

```rs
/// Refresh the boolean value from a parameter block: when the index is
/// nonzero, follow the block's entry table (1-based) to the value slot and
/// store whether it is nonzero; otherwise keep the incoming pointer. Returns
/// the source word with its low byte replaced by the flag, like the original.
export!(thiscall, rw_00648ad0(this: *mut u8, param: *const u8) -> u32 {
    unsafe {
        let index = *(this.add(0x0c) as *const u32);
        let mut source = param as u32;
        if index != 0 {
            let entries = *(param.add(0x14) as *const *const u32);

            source = *(slot as *const u32);
        }
        let flag = (source != 0) as u32;
        *this.add(0x20) = flag as u8;
        (source & !0xFF) | flag
    }
});
```

```rs
/// Float degree-of-freedom "adopt if larger" step.
///
/// If the square of the candidate value exceeds the square of the given
/// limit, copies the candidate value into this object and copies the
/// candidate's validity bit into this object's tag byte. Returns the
/// candidate pointer, matching the value the original leaves in EAX.
export!(thiscall, rw_00684480(this_: *mut u8, other: *const u8, limit: f32) -> u32 {
```

```rs
// original: 0x00684730 rage::crFrameDofInt::vf7
/// Integer degree-of-freedom scale step.
///
/// Multiplies the live integer (converted to float) by the factor and
/// truncates back to an integer. Matches the original's truncate
/// instruction exactly: NaN and positive overflow produce 0x80000000
/// (Rust's saturating cast already yields 0x80000000 for negative
/// overflow, so only the other two cases need a guard). Returns the result.
export!(thiscall, rw_00684730(this_: *mut u8, factor: f32) -> u32 {
    unsafe {
        let slot = this_.add(VALUE_OFF) as *mut i32;
        let scaled = (*slot as f32) * factor;
        let out: u32 = if scaled.is_nan() || scaled >= 2147483648.0 {
            0x8000_0000
        } else {
            scaled as i32 as u32
        };
        *slot = out as i32;
        out
    }
});
```

```rs
// original: 0x00684880 cr_frame_dof_init_by_kind
/// Degree-of-freedom kind initializer.
///
/// Tags the object for one of four kinds (0-3): writes the kind's vtable
/// pointer at +0 and the tag byte 0x10+kind at +4. A null object or a kind
/// above 3 leaves memory untouched. Returns the low byte of the kind.
/// The vtable immediates carry loader fixups, so they are relocated.
export!(thiscall, rw_00684880(this_: *mut u8, kind: u32) -> u32 {
    unsafe {
        let k = (kind & 0xFF) as u8;
        if k <= 3 && !this_.is_null() {
            let (tag, vfptr) = match k {
                0 => (0x10u8, 0x00E9_5580u32),
                1 => (0x11u8, 0x00E9_55BCu32),
                2 => (0x12u8, 0x00EC_B95Cu32),
                _ => (0x13u8, 0x00FE_386Cu32),
            };
            *this_.add(TAG_OFF) = tag;
            *(this_ as *mut u32) = relocated(vfptr);
        }
        kind & 0xFF
    }
});
```

`rewrites/pending/functions/fn_006848f0.rs`:

```rs
// original: 0x006848f0 indexed_word_fetch
/// Indexed word fetch from a strided table.
///
/// Reads the flag word at +0x1c: when bit 1 is clear, stores the index
/// itself into the output slot. Otherwise bounds-checks the index against
/// the u16 limit at +0x14 (out of range returns 0 and writes nothing) and
/// copies the u16 at table[index * 0xE0 + 0x16] into the output slot,
/// returning 1. The full EAX value on each path matches the original.
export!(thiscall, rw_006848f0(this_: *const u8, index: u32, out: *mut u16) -> u32 {
    unsafe {
        const STRIDE: usize = 0xE0;
        const ENTRY_OFF: usize = 0x16;
        let idx = (index & 0xFFFF) as u16;
        let flags = *(this_.add(0x1C) as *const u32);
        let hi = (flags >> 1) & 0xFFFF_0000;
        if flags & 0x02 == 0 {
            *out = idx;
            return hi | ((idx as u32) & 0xFF00) | 1;
        }
        let bound = *(this_.add(0x14) as *const u16);
        if idx >= bound {
            return hi | ((idx as u32) & 0xFF00);
        }
        let table = *(this_ as *const u32) as *const u8;
        *out = *(table.add(idx as usize * STRIDE + ENTRY_OFF) as *const u16);
        // The original reloads EAX with the output pointer before returning,
        // so EAX carries the output address here, not the table address.
        (out as u32 & 0xFFFF_FF00) | 1
    }
});

```

```rs
/// Query one filter parameter, or fall back to the mode flag.
///
/// `sel` chooses which parameter slot to read (5 -> slot C, 6 -> slot 10);
/// any other value, or a lane id that does not match the object, returns
/// the mode byte instead. On success the value is also written through
/// `out`, and the return is whether it exceeds the shared threshold.
export!(thiscall, rs80_694e90(this: *const u8, sel: u32, lane: u32, out: *mut u32) -> u32 {

        const SLOT_A: u32 = 5;
        let sub = (sel as u8).wrapping_sub(SLOT_A as u8);

        let bits = if sub == 0 && lane_ok {
            Some(*((this).add(0x0C) as *const u32))
        } else if sub == 1 && lane_ok {
            Some(*((this).add(0x10) as *const u32))
        } else {
            None
        };

            Some(b) => {
                *out = b;
                let thresh = f32::from_bits(*global::<u32>(0x00FE8628));
                ((f32::from_bits(b) > thresh) as u8) as u32
            }
            None => *((this).add(0x16)) as u32,
        }
    }
```

```rs
// original: 0x00694ee0 filter_derive_key
/// Derive the filter key by folding four field descriptors through a helper.
///
/// Chains four helper calls over the (offset, size) pairs (C,4), (10,4),
/// (14,2), (16,1), threading the running key through ECX and each field
/// pointer through EDX; returns the final key.
///
/// Note: the helper uses a custom convention (ECX/EDX plus one cdecl stack
/// word), which safe Rust cannot express, so the rewrite passes only the
/// stack word. The checker therefore verifies the call count, order, size
/// arguments and final return; the register threading is structural and is
/// documented here rather than verified.
export!(thiscall, rs80_694ee0(this: *const u8) -> u32 {
    unsafe {
        const FIELDS: [(usize, u32); 4] = [(0x0C, 4), (0x10, 4), (0x14, 2), (0x16, 1)];
        let _ = this;
        let mut acc: u32 = 0;
        for (off, size) in FIELDS {
            let _field_ptr = (this as u32).wrapping_add(off as u32);
            let _ = _field_ptr;
            acc = callee_cdecl!(1, u32, size);
        }
        acc
    }
});
```

```rs
// original: 0x006950b0 channel_store_propagate
/// Store a channel value, optionally propagating it to linked channels.
///
/// Always stores `fbits` at `index` in the value array. When `flag` is
/// nonzero, walks the node graph reachable from the index's node (child at
/// +C, sibling at +8, parent at +10) and stores the same value at each
/// visited node's channel index (+14). Returns nothing meaningful.
export!(thiscall, rs80_6950b0(this: *const u8, index: u32, fbits: u32, flag: u32) -> u32 {
    unsafe {
        let arr = *((this).add(0x0C) as *const u32) as *mut u32;
        *arr.add(index as usize) = fbits;
        if (flag as u8) == 0 {
            return 0; // unchecked: the original leaks entry-EAX on this path
        }
        let node_base = *(((*((this).add(0x14) as *const u32)) as *const u8).add(0) as *const u32);
        let start = node_base.wrapping_add(index.wrapping_mul(0xE0));
        let mut cur = start;
        loop {
            if cur == 0 {
                break;
            }
            let down = *((cur as *const u8).add(0x0C) as *const u32);
            if down != 0 {
                cur = down;
            } else if cur == start {
                cur = 0;
            } else {
                let sib = *((cur as *const u8).add(8) as *const u32);
                if sib != 0 {
                    cur = sib;
                } else {
                    let mut up = *((cur as *const u8).add(0x10) as *const u32);
                    if up == 0 {
                        cur = 0;
                    } else {
                        loop {
                            if *((up as *const u8).add(8) as *const u32) != 0 {
                                break;
                            }
                            if up == start {
                                up = 0;
                                break;
                            }
                            up = *((up as *const u8).add(0x10) as *const u32);
                            if up == 0 {
                                break;
                            }
                        }
                        if up == 0 || up == start {
                            cur = 0;
                        } else {
                            cur = *((up as *const u8).add(8) as *const u32);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            if cur == 0 {
                break;
            }
            let ci = *((cur as *const u8).add(0x14) as *const u16) as usize;
            *arr.add(ci) = fbits;
        }
        0 // unchecked: see contract (return is entry-dependent residue)
    }
});
```

```rs
/// Look up an animation object by id.
///
/// Ids below 0x80 index the direct table. Larger ids scan the overflow
/// entries (slots 14 and up) for a matching leading id byte. Returns the
/// object pointer, or null when absent.
export!(thiscall, rs80_695290(id: u32) -> u32 {

        const DIRECT_MAX: u8 = 0x80;
        const OVERFLOW_FROM: u32 = 14;
        let b = id as u8;
        if b < DIRECT_MAX {
            let table = *global::<u32>(0x019F2380) as *const u32;
            *table.add(b as usize)

            if count <= OVERFLOW_FROM {
                return 0;
            }
            let table = *global::<u32>(0x019F2380) as *const u32;

                let e = *table.add(i as usize);
                if e != 0 && *(e as *const u8) == b {
                    return e;
                }
                i += 1;
            }
            0
        }
    }
});
```

```rs
// original: 0x006957c0 rage::crAnimToleranceSimple::vf1
/// Tolerance lookup: pick a threshold float by (kind, lane).
///
/// Kinds 0 and 5 read the near threshold (slot 4), kinds 1 and 6 the far
/// threshold (slot 8); both fall back to the shared epsilon when the lane
/// is zero. Every other kind reads the default threshold (slot C).
export!(thiscall, rs80_6957c0(this: *const u8, kind: u32, lane: u32, _u: u32) -> f32 {
    unsafe {
        let bits = match kind as u8 {
            0 | 5 => {
                if (lane as u16) == 0 {
```
